item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers look to even up the NLCS in Game 2 against the Milwaukee Brewers. Last night, they fell 0-1 in the series after a 2-1 pitching duel.
The Dodgers offense was nearly nonexistent, leaving nine runners on base and going 1-for-6 with RISP.
In today’s 2:00 P.M. PST game, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made a lineup change involving their best postseason hitter.
Kiké Hernández Out, Tommy Edman In vs. Brewers
Per Los Angeles Dodgers reporter David Vassegh, Kiké Hernández will sit tonight with Tommy Edman taking his place at second and batting ninth.
In five games this postseason, Edman has yet to record hit.
In Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves, Hernández hit a towering two-run home run ultimately lifting the Dodgers to victory.
Aside from that home run, both Edman and Hernández’s bats have been awfully quiet.
But, the NLCS is where Edman shines. In 2024, he won NLCS MVP. Recording 11 RBIS–tying a franchise record–with a home run, and a .407 batting average which included a hit in each game.
Last year against Milwakuee in the NLCS, Edman tallied five hits and three RBIs.
Tonight, the Dodgers need at least one bat to breakout and shift the momentum of the series before heading home for Games 3 through 5.
More on Dodgers: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Intriguing Corey Seager Trade News After NLCS Loss
Dodgers vs. Brewers Game 2 Lineups
Dave Roberts made several slight tweaks aside from the Tommy Edman, Kiké Hernández switch.
Teoscar Hernández moved up to third, while the struggling Will Smith dropped down to fifth.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Yoshinobu Yamamoto Keeps His Approach Steady for NLCS
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto will take the ball Monday against a Brewers lineup he sees as strong from top to bottom. Speaking in Japanese ahead of his Game 2 start, he stressed staying focused, limiting runs and working through hitters one at a time. item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE, WI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto will take the ball Monday against a Brewers lineup he sees as strong from top to bottom. Speaking in Japanese ahead of his Game 2 start, he stressed staying focused, limiting runs and working through hitters one at a time. He also explained how his daily routine helps him get ready to pitch even as his body feels different from day to day. In his third MLB postseason, Yamamoto believes experience can help while his approach to each start stays the same.
Staying sharp against the Brewers
Yamamoto expects Milwaukee to make the Dodgers earn their outs.
“My impression is that they’re a team with very few weaknesses,” he said. “I want to stay focused and pitch well so that we’re careful about making mistakes on our side first.”
Asked about the importance of pitching deep into games, Yamamoto put the focus on the work that gets him there.
“In the postseason, I put more weight on keeping runs to a minimum and retiring each batter one at a time,” he said. “That’s something I value especially in October. I think that leads to pitching deeper into games as a result.”
His aim is to bring the same care to a regular-season start that he brings to an October game.
“I pitch every game during the season with the same mindset as an important game like this,” he said. “For an important postseason game, my mindset is to do what I always do.”
“I’ve valued that approach for years and years. There are failures along the way, but little by little, I feel the number of games in which I’m able to pitch well has grown.”
A routine built over years
Yamamoto’s training routine has drawn plenty of interest. For him, its value comes from the years he has spent following it.
“I’ve been doing the same training since I became a professional at 18,” he said. “I still value it just as much today.”
“I think it’s very important to keep doing the same things every day with the same mindset and the same intensity.”
That steady work helps him prepare through the daily changes in how his body feels.
“Your physical condition is different every day,” Yamamoto said. “Of course, sometimes the differences are small and sometimes they’re large, but your condition changes every day.”
“My routine is about getting myself into the same condition by the time I’m ready to play.”
Experience grows, the mindset stays
Asked about his strong road results, Yamamoto gave a modest answer.
“I’m not doing anything different in particular, and even I don’t really know the exact reason,” he said. “For some reason, the results have been good.”
A reporter also brought up the determination Yamamoto had expressed before last year’s Game 2 against Milwaukee and asked whether another year of experience had changed how he felt.
“My mindset going into a game is always the same,” Yamamoto said. “There’s last year’s experience, and this is my third postseason here, so of course there will be situations where that experience helps.”
“But in terms of how I feel going into the game, it’s the same.”

item.description: 「難しく考える必要はない」スクバル、山本由伸でブルワーズを圧倒 ド軍サイトが描く“理想のシナリオ”「本拠地決着を」 敵地では山本とスクバルが先発予定だ(C)Getty Images 今季も世界一の座に向け、着実にポストシーズンを勝ち上がっているドジャース。ブレーブスとの地区シリーズ（NLDS）を3勝1敗で制し、現地時間10月11日からはブルワーズとのリーグ優勝決定シリーズ（NLCS）がスタートする。昨季と同じカードとなったNLCSでは、ドジャースはタリク・スクバル、山本由伸がそれぞれ敵地での1、2戦目の先発予定として発表されている。7戦4勝制のシリーズにおいて、序盤の先発マウンドが託される球界屈指の両先発投手への期待は膨らむばかりだ。 NLDSでは3戦目に先発した山本が、このブルワーズとのNLCSでは2戦目に先発する。現在のドジャース先発陣において、もっとも信頼出来るスクバルと山本の2人を立てることで、昨年の4連勝突破再現の可能性も高まる。 ドジャース専門サイト『DODGERS NATION』も10日配信のトピックで、スクバル、山本を2戦目までに並べる先発起用に対し、敵地で連勝も狙える
item.content:encoded:
「難しく考える必要はない」スクバル、山本由伸でブルワーズを圧倒 ド軍サイトが描く“理想のシナリオ”「本拠地決着を」
敵地では山本とスクバルが先発予定だ(C)Getty Images
今季も世界一の座に向け、着実にポストシーズンを勝ち上がっているドジャース。ブレーブスとの地区シリーズ（NLDS）を3勝1敗で制し、現地時間10月11日からはブルワーズとのリーグ優勝決定シリーズ（NLCS）がスタートする。昨季と同じカードとなったNLCSでは、ドジャースはタリク・スクバル、山本由伸がそれぞれ敵地での1、2戦目の先発予定として発表されている。7戦4勝制のシリーズにおいて、序盤の先発マウンドが託される球界屈指の両先発投手への期待は膨らむばかりだ。
NLDSでは3戦目に先発した山本が、このブルワーズとのNLCSでは2戦目に先発する。現在のドジャース先発陣において、もっとも信頼出来るスクバルと山本の2人を立てることで、昨年の4連勝突破再現の可能性も高まる。
ドジャース専門サイト『DODGERS NATION』も10日配信のトピックで、スクバル、山本を2戦目までに並べる先発起用に対し、敵地で連勝も狙える「強力な組み合わせ」と評価。さらに、「ドジャースとデーブ・ロバーツ監督は、この決断について難しく考える必要はなかっただろう」と綴っている。
また、初戦先発予定のスクバルがシーズンを通して、敵地で好結果を残していると説明。同メディアは、「2026年シーズン、スクバルは本拠地での14試合の先発で防御率3.63だった一方、敵地での12試合では防御率1.70を記録している」と今季の成績を紹介し、その上で、「仮に第1戦が思い通りの結果にならなかったとしても、ドジャースには敵地で行われる第2戦に、とっておきのエースが控えている」と論じている。

item.title: [Heavy.com] Milwaukee Brewers Manager Takes Shot at Tarik Skubal Before NLCS Game One
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are set for a battle in the National League Championship Series. Game One kicks off the potential seven-game series with perhaps the best pitching matchup of the entire MLB season between 2X Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski. Ahead of the star-studded pitching matchup, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy took a shot at Skubal in a bizarre way. More MLB on Heavy: Anthony Volpe Sounds Off On New York Ya
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are set for a battle in the National League Championship Series.
Game One kicks off the potential seven-game series with perhaps the best pitching matchup of the entire MLB season between 2X Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski.
Ahead of the star-studded pitching matchup, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy took a shot at Skubal in a bizarre way.
More MLB on Heavy: Anthony Volpe Sounds Off On New York Yankees with 2-Word Message
Pat Murphy Takes Jab At Tarik Skubal
There’s no doubt that Tarik Skubal is a very stingy pitcher, and it’s very hard to string together success against him, especially in the playoffs.
Skubal has rounded into postseason form over his last handful of starts (Which included a strong Game 1 start against the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS), and looks to be at his peak at the right time.
Per @DodgersNation, Pat Murphy said this about how to beat Skubal:
“Step on his throat… Respectfully.”
“I mean that respectfully because I really like Tarik. My brain can’t go any place else. Go to work, that’s the only mentality I can have.”
It’s a pretty bizarre statement to make before facing a pitcher, but it shows how intense Murphy is and how fired up he is for this matchup.
More MLB on Heavy: Pat Murphy Sounds Off On Tarik Skubal Before Dodgers-Brewers NLCS
Dodgers Set for Battle In NLCS with Brewers
The Milwaukee Brewers are clearly coming into this NLCS with a bit of an edge in terms of being fired up for the matchup.
That’s not to say that the Dodgers aren’t amped up, because they very much are, but after LA swept the Brewers in the 2025 NLCS, it’s hard to think that the Brewers haven’t been thinking about that all year, and in terms of regular-season wins, Milwaukee had an even better campaign in 2026.
However, this Dodgers team is absolutely battle-tested, and they are set up perfectly for another World Series run.
Having Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitching games one and two, and once the series shifts to LA after two games, will allow some comfort for starters Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow to pitch at home, which might be a huge boost in the series for the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Kyle Tucker Decision Before NLCS Game 1

item.title: [LancasterOnline] Christian Yelich and the Brewers looking to get past Shohei Ohtani and the Dodgers in NLCS sequel
item.dc:creator: JAY COHEN
item.description: MILWAUKEE (AP) — All along, Christian Yelich felt this was going to be part of the road for the Milwaukee Brewers. It was always going to be the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers — with their consecutive World Series titles and a payroll that casts a long shadow over Yelich and the small-market Brewers. “We’ve been expecting having to play them in this round since spring training, in the regular season,” Yelich said Saturday. “You kind of just know that’s what’s going to happen.” The 2026 NL Championsh
item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — All along, Christian Yelich felt this was going to be part of the road for the Milwaukee Brewers.
It was always going to be the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers — with their consecutive World Series titles and a payroll that casts a long shadow over Yelich and the small-market Brewers.
“We’ve been expecting having to play them in this round since spring training, in the regular season,” Yelich said Saturday. “You kind of just know that’s what’s going to happen.”
The 2026 NL Championship Series is a sequel, with Shohei Ohtani and the Dodgers taking on Jackson Chourio and the Brewers. Los Angeles swept Milwaukee in last year's NLCS on the way to the franchise's 26th NL pennant and ninth World Series championship. The Dodgers also eliminated the Brewers in the NLCS in 2018 and the wild-card round in 2020.
Game 1 on Sunday night features a pair of stingy aces. Tarik Skubal goes for Los Angeles after the two-time Cy Young Award winner was acquired in an Aug. 1 trade with Detroit, and Jacob Misiorowski — the front-runner for the NL Cy Young Award — starts for Milwaukee.
The return engagement for the NLCS also shines a light on the competing arguments at the center of MLB's collective bargaining negotiations. Baseball’s five-year labor contract expires Dec. 1, and management is expected to lock out players in a confrontation that could affect the 2027 season.
The Dodgers went 100-62 this season and won the NL West for the fifth straight year after they had an opening-day payroll of $323.6 million, second only to the New York Mets. Milwaukee's opening-day payroll of $125.9 million ranked 20th, and the Brewers set a franchise record with a major league-best 103 wins on the way to their fourth consecutive Central title.
“We’re focused on trying to win, and I think we have for a while,” Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said. “Regardless of what the economics look like, the guys in there believe, and so do I.”
Milwaukee was shut down by Los Angeles in last year's playoffs, hitting .118 while managing just one run in each game in the sweep. Ohtani punctuated the series by swatting three solo homers and striking out 10 over six shutout innings in Game 4.
Ohtani won't pitch this time around because of injuries, and the Japanese slugger went 2 for 13 with four strikeouts in the four-game NL Division Series against Atlanta. But the Dodgers still have a formidable rotation, fronted by Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
“Every night when you play these guys, you know you’re going to face a great pitcher, a Cy Young-caliber pitcher,” Yelich said.

The Dodgers announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 on Sunday, while the Brewers announced Saturday that they will have ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. Both teams clinched their spot in the NLCS on Thursday, the Brewers with a 3-1 win over the Padres and the Dodgers with a 4-1 win over the Braves.
Misiorowski pitched just once in the series, throwing four innings of two-run ball in Game 1. Similarly, Skubal opened things against the Braves, going six innings with just one run allowed, and did not pitch again. Both should be well-rested.
The most realistic argument against a Skubal-Misiorowski duel lies in October superstar Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but the Dodgers righty pitched in Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, meaning he’d start Sunday on just four days’ rest. He will pitch in Game 2 on Monday with a regular recovery that would make more sense.
We’ve seen great pitching in the 2026 postseason thus far and several marquee matchups: Cam Schlittler vs. Payton Tolle; Chris Sale vs. Jesús Luzardo; Max Fried vs. Sonny Gray; Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen; Yamamoto vs. Sale.
But Skubal vs. Misiorowski will take the cake.
After some struggles late in the regular season, Misiorowski pitched behind an opener when he made his postseason debut a year ago, but he was effective in three appearances. He allowed only one run across seven innings in the NLDS against the Cubs, before striking out nine and yielding just one run in five innings against the Dodgers in the NLCS.
But this is not the same Miz in 2026. The flame-throwing 24-year-old finished the regular season with MLB bests in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), WHIP (0.80) and opponents’ batting average (.157). It was more than a breakout -- it was among the greatest pitching seasons in MLB history.
Misiorowski’s four-seam fastball topped out at 104.8 mph and averaged 101.2 mph against the Padres in the NLDS. With the adrenaline that is sure to be present on Sunday, who knows what eye-popping numbers he could put up.
As for Skubal, he won’t win a third consecutive Cy Young. But that won’t take away from the 2.72 ERA he posted in 26 starts, including a 2.61 mark after his blockbuster trade to the Dodgers. Remember, too, that Skubal missed 44 days in the summer after he needed surgery to remove loose bodies in his left elbow. There have been few signs of rust from that recovery.
Skubal’s strong playoff debut with the Dodgers was just more of what we’re used to from the southpaw. He made six postseason starts as a Tiger in 2024 and 2025 with a 2.04 ERA, never going shorter than six innings and allowing more than two runs just once.
The Brewers and Dodgers will already provide appointment viewing throughout the NLCS, a rematch of the 2025 NL pennant battle and a meeting of MLB’s top regular-season teams in 2026. Add in the bout of Misiorowski and Skubal in Game 1, and this series should get off to an awfully hot start.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, will start Game 2 on Monday at American Family Field, manager Dave Roberts said Friday.
Skubal also started Game 1 of the NL Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-hander struck out seven and walked two.
Yamamoto started Game 3 of the NLDS, and struck out 10 over seven innings. The right-hander allowed one run and four hits to go with one walk.
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell struggled as the Game 2 starter against the Braves, who won 3-2 to tie the best-of-five series 1-1. The Dodgers went on to eliminate the Braves, 3-1.
Roberts said the Dodgers were in discussions about adding a pitcher for the best-of-seven NLCS, which would require them to drop a position player. Rosters are due Sunday morning.
Miguel Rojas exited Game 3 against the Braves during an at-bat with lower back pain. The utility player underwent imaging, which mostly showed prior back issues. He took ground balls and a couple rounds of batting practice at Dodger Stadium on Friday.
Rojas, 37, has said he's leaning toward retiring at the end of the season.
“Today was encouraging,” Roberts said. “We still have a flight to get on and see how he comes in tomorrow for the workout there, so there’s nothing definitive.”

item.content:encoded:
相手打者を寄せ付けない支配力が称賛を集めている。現地時間10月6日に行われたブレーブスとのナ・リーグ地区シリーズ第3戦に登板した山本由伸の投球だ。
【動画】えぐいキレ！山本由伸がスプリットで空振り三振を奪うシーンをチェック
勝った方が王手となる第3戦で、相手エースのクリス・セールとの投げ合い――。否が応でも緊張感が高まる舞台で28歳の日本人エースは真価を発揮した。「ヨシはやってくれる」（デーブ・ロバーツ監督談）と抜群の信頼を寄せられた先発マウンドに立った山本は、7回（98球）を投げ、10奪三振、1失点と好投。ドジャースが勝ち抜けを決めた同シリーズにおいて、流れをグッと手繰り寄せる勝利に貢献した。
2023年オフに大谷翔平を除いて投手史上最高額となる12年3億2500万ドル（約463億円＝当時のレート）の超大型契約を締結した山本。その価値を存分に示しているパフォーマンスには賛辞が止む気配はない。
そんな山本の投球はメジャーリーグの酸いも甘いも知る者たちの目にはどう映っているのだろうか。18年のキャリアを重ねた現役時代にMLBで通算200勝、そして2202奪三振を挙げた大投手のアダム・ウェインライト氏は、米野球専門YouTubeチャンネル『Foul Territory』において「今のヤマモトは時代を代表する投手の一人だ」と強調。昨秋のワールドシリーズで球界の常識を覆す“中0日連投”をやってのけた怪腕のタフネスをクローズアップした。
「あれは私の人生において見たことがない投球だった。これは投手をやったことがある人間以外には分からないだろうけど、ポストシーズンで先発した翌日は普通なら象に踏みつぶされたような感覚になるんだ。本当にそうなんだ。それなのにヤマモトは次の日も投げた。しかも、10年契約という重圧を背負いながらだ。そういうタフな姿をこのポストシーズンでも彼は見せている。もっと彼がどれだけ凄い勝負師なのかが広まるべきだ」
また、ドジャースOBで、現役時代にMLBで204勝を挙げた大投手のオーレル・ハーシュハイザー氏は、米スポーツ専門局『ESPN LA』の番組内で、山本の“ミスの少なさ”に言及した。
「彼は普段から制球が抜群だ。コントロールが優れていれば、4つ、あるいは5つの球種を使って打者の弱点をあらゆる攻め方ができる。ただ、私が特に感銘を受けるのは、内角へのストレートだ。ポストシーズンのような舞台で内角に投げるのはどんな投手でも多少なりとも怖さがある。一振りで仕留められる危険があるからね。メジャーリーグは誰にでもその力はある。でも、ヤマモトは重要な場面でこそ、際どい内角へのストレートを投げる。しかもミスなくね。本当に集中しきっていたんだ」
百戦錬磨の名投手たちがこぞって讃える山本。その現状からして一部で批判も頂戴した12年3億2500万ドルの契約の価値はあったと言えよう。
[文/構成:ココカラネクスト編集部]

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers will have time to reset rotation, bullpen, and struggling Shohei Ohtani for NLCS
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5.
By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game.
"It's important. It was very important," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Once you get to an elimination game, a Game 5 or a Game 7, anything can happen. And to be able to win today, get back, reset, have a day off tomorrow, set the rotation, it's huge."
The extra rest means Tarik Skubal likely will be the choice to start against Milwaukee instead of handling a Game 5 against the Braves. Similarly, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow will be well rested for their expected NLCS starts.
Infielder Miguel Rojas may need the extra rest for a sore lower back that kept him out.
Also, Edwin Díaz will have ample time to reset after recording saves on back-to-back days to close out the series against Atlanta. The ninth-inning work showed Díaz is re-established as the closer.
"The team trusts me," Díaz said. "I think that was the most important thing for me, the team trusts me. They give me the ball every single day. And the last two nights it's been amazing. That's why I came here to win games and close games like this one. So I'm really happy right now."
Despite those advantages, Roberts is preparing for a tough NLCS as the Dodgers try to move closer to their goal of becoming the first NL team to win three consecutive World Series.
"We've got our work cut out," Roberts said, adding extra rest also will be important for such players as Ohtani and Freddie Freeman.
Ohtani was 2 for 13 against Atlanta and hasn't homered since Aug. 18 while dealing with injuries to his right biceps, left knee and neck that have also kept the two-way player off the mound.
"So kind of enjoy this one, get Shohei a couple of days to get back," Roberts said. "Freddie, he had a big series, but, again a couple of days will help him. Give our guys in the 'pen a little reset. So we'll be ready to go Game 1."
Díaz pitched a perfect ninth inning in the clinching win. The on-field celebration was a low-key affair, but Roberts and his players, wearing "Take October" T-shirts and goggles to protect their eyes, soon were drenched with champagne.
The Dodgers made the most of their opportunity to celebrate another postseason series win while maintaining their focus on a third straight World Series championship.
"Our goal is to win the World Series, not this series," Díaz said. "We've got eight more wins to go. So our goal is win those eight games. And at the end of the day when we win those eight games, we celebrate.
"Now we're going back to LA to keep working. I know all the guys are on the same track. Now we just celebrate a little bit, go back to LA, get working and be ready for Sunday."
Andy Pages' bases-loaded single in the seventh drove in two runs to give the Dodgers a 3-1 lead. Max Muncy added to the lead with a homer in the ninth, his third blast of the postseason.
"Obviously, we have big teams, big series coming up," Pages said. "We're going to face tough teams, so prepare for those moments, but also take advantage of the opportunity of being here and enjoying these moments. And knowing that our ultimate goal is to win the World Series. So focus on that."

item.content:encoded:
Oct 7, 2026, 10:01 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz picked up his second save in as many nights on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with a strikeout in his team's 4-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series. Diaz missed most of the 2026 regular season due to elbow and neck injuries. However, he's been dominant since returning from the injured list in mid-September. Diaz allowed just two baserunners while notching nine strikeouts in his final five innings pitched of the regular season, and he's now logged low-stress saves in each of his first two appearances of the playoffs. With Diaz rounding into form, Los Angeles' bullpen looks like a major strength heading into the National League Championship Series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
More Recent News
Oct 7, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians left-hander Foster Griffin was dominant in a bulk relief appearance in his team's 9-3 win over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Griffin followed Cleveland opener Daniel Espino and allowed two hits and one earned run while striking out seven across 2 2/3 innings of work. The 31-year-old was used exclusively as a starting pitcher during the regular season, posting a 15-6 record with a 3.60 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, and 158 strikeouts across 172 2/3 innings (31 starts) split between the Guardians and the Washington Nationals. However, Griffin struggled mightily late in the year, pitching to a 5.05 ERA in the second half and a 6.87 ERA across 18 1/3 innings in September. If Griffin can rediscover his early-season form in a bullpen role, he could help Cleveland mount a comeback in the ALDS.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians outfielder Jo Adell had a big night in his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, going two-for-four with a walk and three RBI. With the game tied 1-1 in the third inning, Adell put the Guardians ahead for good with a three-run triple off of White Sox left-hander Hagen Smith. Across 660 regular-season plate appearances split between the Guardians and the Los Angeles Angels, Adell hit .240/.298/.401 with 23 home runs, 94 RBI, 70 runs scored, and five stolen bases. He was better with Cleveland than he was with Los Angeles, posting a .740 OPS across 204 trips to the plate after the Guardians acquired him at the trade deadline. Adell has notched a couple of key hits for Cleveland in the ALDS and now has four RBI across the first three games of the series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages had the key hit in his team's 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday, logging a go-ahead two-run single off Braves right-hander Robert Suarez in the seventh inning. Pages finished the game with two hits and two RBI in three at-bats. The 25-year-old was a critical piece of the Dodgers lineup during the regular season, hitting .274 with 23 home runs, 85 RBI, 75 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases. However, Pages struggled mightily during the Dodgers' run to the 2025 World Series, notching just four hits in 55 postseason plate appearances. After his big night on Wednesday, Pages has already logged four hits in just 15 plate appearances in the 2026 playoffs.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:19 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith was lights out to secure his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Smith entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded the final six outs, logging five strikeouts without allowing a single baserunner. The 27-year-old was one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, pitching to a 1.95 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 107 strikeouts and 41 saves across 74 innings (69 games). Smith has been dominant so far in the Division Series as well, as he's yet to allow a hit or a walk in his four innings of work. If Cleveland is going to mount a comeback in the series, it will likely need Smith to continue his dominance.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:11 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was one of the stars of his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series. In five plate appearances, Ramirez recorded a double, a triple, a walk, two RBI, two runs scored, and a stolen base. With Cleveland leading 5-3 in the 8th inning, it was Ramirez's two-run triple that sealed the win for the Guardians and kept the series alive to see Game 4. The 34-year-old battled through injuries and underperformance in 2026, hitting .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs, 53 RBI, 71 runs scored, and 37 stolen bases across 544 plate appearances. Ramirez also got off to a slow start in the postseason, going hitless in his first eight trips to the plate against the White Sox. If Cleveland is going to rally all the way back from two games down in the ALDS, it will need Ramirez to stay hot in Games 4 and 5.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Robert Gasser Starting Game 4 of NLDS Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:08 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser will start for the Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres, according to Brewers reporter Sophia Minnaert. It will be Gasser's first career postseason start after throwing 2 2/3 innings of relief in the playoffs for the Brew Crew last year. The 27-year-old southpaw went 5-5 on the season with a 3.87 ERA (4.24 FIP) and 1.19 WHIP with a career-high 103 strikeouts and 35 walks in 109 1/3 innings across 21 appearances (20 starts). The problem for Gasser is that he has not made a start in almost two weeks, so he could be a bit rusty. Manager Pat Murphy will surely have a short hook on the young left-hander as the Brewers look to close the best-of-five series out in San Diego. Gasser was outstanding down the stretch in 2026, allowing two earned runs or fewer in each of his last six starts, walking 12 and striking out 31 in 32 1/3 innings during that span. He did not face the Padres at all during the regular season, which could give him a bit of an advantage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sophia Minnaert
Mason Miller Back From the Paternity List for Game 4


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:03 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced on Wednesday that they returned right-handed closer Mason Miller from the paternity list, taking the place on the National League Division Series roster of left-handed reliever Wandy Peralta. Miller blew a two-inning save in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee against the Brewers and was then unavailable for the win in Game 3 at Petco Park on Tuesday night. It is great news for the Padres, who did not have left-handed high-leverage reliever Adrian Morejon on Tuesday due to a left-shoulder issue. The Padres had to go to Game 1 starter, right-hander Michael King, for the two-inning save with both Miller and Morejon unavailable. It is uncertain if Morejon will be able to pitch late in the game in another must-win contest on Wednesday in Game 4, but the Padres will at least have their stud closer back in the fold. The two-time All-Star was lights-out during the regular season, his first full season with the Friars, posting a 1.67 ERA (1.17 FIP), 0.900 WHIP, a career-high and league-high 38 saves, a career-high 129 strikeouts, and 26 walks in just 70 innings pitched. With their season on the line, expect manager Craig Stammen to be aggressive in his usage of Miller if Game 4 is close in the later innings, even though he showed command issues in the ninth on Sunday in Milwaukee.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Miguel Rojas Not Worried About Back/Hip Injury


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 12:28 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back, hip) said he felt some tightness in his left lower-back/hip area during a swing in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday against the hosting Atlanta Braves before he was pulled mid at-bat, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. However, Rojas was not concerned about his availability for the rest of the series and going forward. Rojas probably will not be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 4 of the series on Wednesday at Truist Park against Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, but it sounds like he should be available off the bench. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder has made two starts so far in the NLDS against the Braves and has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout. He was hitless in three at-bats with a strikeout in Tuesday's Game 3 win before being replaced at second base by Tommy Edman. Rojas has mostly been a bench player for the Dodgers in his 13th year in the league (fourth with L.A.) in 2026, but he proved in last year's World Series that he is still capable of coming through in the clutch when needed. He hit .267 (60-for-225) with four homers and 23 RBI during the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Oct 7, 2026, 11:57 AM ET
St. Louis Cardinals right-handed closer Riley O'Brien was a first-time All-Star in 2026 in his first full season as the team's closer, and he ended the year tied with San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller for the National League lead in saves (38) with a 4.08 ERA across a career-high 64 innings pitched. O'Brien also set a career high in appearances (66) in his first full year as a big-leaguer. He did not allow an earned run in his first 13 appearances of the year and ended the first half with a 3.43 ERA and a 7.9% walk rate in 39 1/3 frames. O'Brien had 24 saves in his first 28 opportunities. But in 27 appearances after the All-Star break, O'Brien had a 5.11 ERA in 24 2/3 innings, and his walk rate rose to 14.4% while he went 14-for-18 in save chances. Three of his blown saves in the second half came in September, and five of his losing decisions came in his final 13 outings. The 31-year-old said he experienced "fatigue" in the closing days of the season and that his legs have "been feeling heavy compared to how they felt early in the year," according to Daniel Guerrero of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. As he tired, the velocity of O'Brien's pitches suffered. To be able to maintain velocity through the entire season, O'Brien said he plans to focus on putting on "as much muscle as I can."--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Daniel Guerrero
Curtis Mead the Favorite to Start at Second Base Next Year


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Boston Red Sox infielder Curtis Mead is considered the favorite to open next season as the team's starting second baseman, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline this summer, but he ended up playing in only one game for Boston due to a fractured wrist that he suffered in his second at-bat with the team. The 25-year-old will now have all offseason to heal up, and he will enter spring training as the team's primary option at the keystone as they attempt to get back to the playoffs in 2027. The Australian native was having a breakout 2026 campaign with the Nationals before being traded to Boston, and he finished the year with a .253/.353/.498 slash line with an .851 OPS, 17 home runs, 48 RBI, 49 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 285 at-bats in 88 combined games with Washington and Boston. "That would be, I would say, broadly our plan," said manager Chad Tracy when asked about second base. "He was acquired for a reason. You see the numbers that kind of project at least toward a 30-home run season. And adding that, we were really excited about that."--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Walker Buehler to Start Game 4 of NLDS Against Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:36 AM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that veteran right-hander Walker Buehler will make the start in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Buehler will make his first postseason appearance this year after going 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA (4.51 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 131 strikeouts and 57 walks in 153 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts for the Padres in his first season with the team. The 32-year-old is no longer the high-end ace that he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he does have plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA (3.21 FIP) with 114 strikeouts and 36 walks in 94 2/3 innings pitched. Buehler's last start came on Sept. 26 against the division-rival Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed four runs (three earned) with a walk and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings for a no-decision. He picked up a win in his only outing against Milwaukee in 2026, giving up just one earned run with two walks and five strikeouts in six innings at Petco Park back on Aug. 11. Buehler will most definitely be on a short leash in a must-win game for San Diego if he is not on his game early on.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Padres PR

Keith Hernandez

San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon (shoulder) was unavailable in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Tuesday night against the Milwaukee Brewers due to "stickiness in his shoulder," manager Craig Stammen told AJ Cassavell of MLB.com. There is still a chance that Morejon will be available for Game 4 against the Brewers in San Diego on Wednesday night as the Friars attempt to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee on Friday night. With Morejon unavailable and closer Mason Miller on the paternity list, the Padres' bullpen was very short on Tuesday night, but Game 1 starter Michael King came to the rescue and threw the final two innings for SD to pick up a save in the 4-3 victory. Morejon has already had two two-inning appearances in this postseason, once in the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs and again on Saturday against the Brewers in Game of the NLDS, when he allowed the game-winning home run to catcher William Contreras. The hard-throwing Cuban left-hander was one of the most effective late-inning setup men during the regular season, though, going 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, three saves, and a career-high 107 strikeouts in just 86 innings out of the bullpen. With Miller unlikely to be back with the team on Wednesday, the Padres could really use Morejon's left arm on Wednesday evening.--Keith Hernandez

Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was one of the stars of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday. Freeman had just one hit in four plate appearances, but it was a solo home run off Braves ace Chris Sale. Freeman put together another strong regular season in 2026, hitting .288/.362/.430 with 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 74 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. The 37-year-old's production tailed off late in the year, as he hit just .184 in September and slugged just one home run across 249 plate appearances after the All-Star break. However, Freeman has looked like his vintage self so far this postseason. Across the first three games of the NLDS, Freeman has logged four hits, two home runs, two RBI, and three runs scored.--Will Brady

Los Angeles Dodgers utility man Enrique Hernandez struck one of the big blows of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, clubbing a two-run home run off of Braves ace Chris Sale to open the scoring in the fourth inning. It was Hernandez's only hit of the night, but it helped the Dodgers chase Sale out of the game after just five innings of work. Hernandez missed a large chunk of the regular season with an oblique injury and was not particularly effective when healthy, hitting .222 with four home runs across 96 plate appearances. However, the 35-year-old has a long history as an unlikely postseason hero. Across 332 career plate appearances in the playoffs, Hernandez has now hit .272 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.--Will Brady

Oct 6, 2026, 10:30 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander Edwin Diaz notched his first save of the 2026 postseason on Tuesday, shutting the door in his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. Diaz allowed a leadoff double to Braves second baseman Ozzie Albies but rallied to retire the next three batters he faced. The 2026 regular season was largely lost to injury for Diaz, who spent time on the injured list due to both elbow and neck issues. However, the 32-year-old closed the season strong after returning from the neck injury in mid-September, allowing just one hit and one walk while recording nine strikeouts across his final five innings (five games) of the year. If Diaz can rediscover his peak form in October, he could be an impact arm for the Dodgers at the end of games.--Will Brady

Yamamoto was dominant during the regular season, recording a 14-9 record with a 2.53 ERA, 0.87 WHIP, and 182 strikeouts across 185 innings (28 starts). He's also been remarkably effective in the postseason to this point in his career, logging an 8-1 record with a 2.14 ERA, 0.83 WHIP, and 58 strikeouts across 63 innings. Following Yamamoto's gem, the Dodgers will have a chance to close out Atlanta in Game 4 and advance to the National League Championship Series on Wednesday.--Will Brady

Miller blew a save opportunity in San Diego's Game 2 loss to the Brewers, allowing a walk-off, two-run single to Milwaukee outfielder Jackson Chourio. Still, the hard-throwing right-hander was one of the best relievers in baseball in the regular season. Without Miller, San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon could be the next man up in the ninth inning for the Padres.--Will Brady

item.title: [New York Post] Doctober classic propels Dodgers to NLCS in quest for World Series three-peat
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate. So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches? So what if he was still in the fifth inning? Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances. Calling on Alex Vesia to record the final out of the inning, Roberts initiated a chaotic sequence of events that resulted in the Dodgers claiming a 4-1 victory over the Braves in Game 4 of their National League Division Series. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate.
So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches?
So what if he was still in the fifth inning?
Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances.
Calling on Alex Vesia to record the final out of the inning, Roberts initiated a chaotic sequence of events that resulted in the Dodgers claiming a 4-1 victory over the Braves in Game 4 of their National League Division Series.
The Dodgers advanced to the NL Championship Series.
Because of Tarik Skubal.
Because of Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
Because of Freddie Freeman.
And because of David Ray Roberts, the manager affectionately known as Doc who has a game or two like this every October.
The victory over the Braves on Wednesday was a Doctober classic.
On a day in which one of his four aces lasted only 4 ⅔ innings, Roberts figured out how to cover 13 outs of the game with a notoriously unpredictable bullpen.
Roberts’ fingerprints were also all over Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning that broke open the game.
When Teoscar Hernandez singled that inning with one out, Braves manager Walt Weiss replaced starting pitcher Tyler Mahle with right-hander Didier Fuentes.
Fuentes forced Max Muncy to ground out, but Hernandez advanced to second base on the play.
Due up was Game 3 hero Kike Hernandez.
Rather than have the right-handed utilityman face Fuentes, Roberts deployed rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch hitter. The left-handed-hitting De Paula drew a walk, at which point he was replaced on the basepaths by Tommy Edman.
Kyle Tucker followed up with another walk to load the bases, at which point Weiss turned to fireballer Robert Suarez to pitch to Pages.
Pages batted .078 in the postseason last year, which resulted in his benching in the World Series. He was 0-for-7 in the first two games of this series, but Roberts stuck with him.
Roberts’ faith was rewarded by the most important hit of Pages’ three-year career, a single to right field that drove in two runs to push the Dodgers in front, 3-1. The runs were the Dodgers’ first of the series that weren’t scored via a home run.
The manager demonstrated an equal level of creativity in directing his bullpen.
Vesia returned for the sixth inning, only to give up a leadoff double to Ozzie Albies. Roberts kept the left-hander in for another batter, the left-handed-hitting Drake Baldwin, who lined out.
Roberts’ next call to the bullpen was for Edgardo Henriquez, who spent the last two weeks of the regular season on the injured list. Henriquez gave up a run in the Dodgers’ Game 2 loss, but not only did Roberts trust him to prevent Albies from scoring, he also had him pitch the seventh inning.
From there, it was simple.
Tanner Scott pitched the eighth inning. With Muncy homering in the ninth inning to increase the lead to 4-1, Edwin Diaz came in to record the last three outs.
The Dodgers moved to within four wins of playing in their third consecutive World Series, and they did it with Shohei Ohtani still missing in action.
Ohtani was 2-for-13 in this series.
“It’s good to know that we can still win games without him doing a whole bunch,” Roberts said. “But he’s going to come to life. It will happen.”
Roberts has squinted extra hard in recent days to find evidence of that.
Here’s the reality: In his last 22 combined games between the regular season and playoffs, Ohtani has no home runs and only one RBI.
That isn’t a slump.
The No. 1 player in the game doesn’t go this long without hitting in the prime of his career without something being seriously wrong with him.
Ohtani spent 15 days last month on the injured list because of a discomfort in his right arm. A couple of days before he was placed on the IL, he said his left knee was also bothering him.
The uncertainty over Ohtani’s capabilities forced Roberts to move him around the lineup.
With Mookie Betts grinding out quality at-bats as the leadoff hitter and Freeman producing enough to solidify his place as the team’s No. 2 hitter, Ohtani was removed from the top of the order.
Against the left-handed Chris Sale in Game 3, Ohtani batted fifth. Against the right-handed Mahle on Wednesday, he batted cleanup.
Ohtani managed to create something out of nothing in the second inning. He drew a walk, then stole second base, prompting Braves catcher Sean Murphy to airmail a throw into center field. Ohtani scampered to third base. When Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubón dropped a popup by Muncy in shallow left field, Ohtani scored to tie the game at 1.
Ohtani didn’t collect any hits Wednesday, but he didn’t have to.
Roberts had the game under control.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Andy Pages comes through in the clutch to send Dodgers to NLCS
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: ATLANTA — Overmatched last postseason and benched during the World Series, Andy Pages used the embarrassment to fuel an All-Star season in 2026. But he was hit by a pitch on Aug. 21 that broke a bone in his hand, didn’t return until the final six games of the regular season and started the postseason, trying to do too much (by his manager’s estimation) to make up for last fall’s lack of contributions. The accounts have been reconciled. It was Pages’ clutch two-out, two-run single in the seventh
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Overmatched last postseason and benched during the World Series, Andy Pages used the embarrassment to fuel an All-Star season in 2026.
But he was hit by a pitch on Aug. 21 that broke a bone in his hand, didn’t return until the final six games of the regular season and started the postseason, trying to do too much (by his manager’s estimation) to make up for last fall’s lack of contributions.
The accounts have been reconciled. It was Pages’ clutch two-out, two-run single in the seventh inning that broke a tie and lifted the Dodgers to a 4-1 victory on Wednesday night in Game 4 of their National League Division Series with the Atlanta Braves.
The victory sends the Dodgers to the National League Championship Series against either the Milwaukee Brewers or San Diego Padres. The Dodgers have reached baseball’s Final Four for the fifth time in the past seven years, the eighth time in the past 11. Their quest for a ‘three-peat’ will continue Sunday either in Milwaukee or at home against the Padres.
This series was decided in the seventh inning.
With the score tied 1-1, Teoscar Hernandez – fresh off a collision with the left field wall that left him on the warning track dirt, rubbing the left side of his head – singled with one out off Braves starter Tyler Mahle. It was just the third hit off Mahle and it came on just his 85th pitch. But Braves manager Walt Weiss went to his bullpen, bringing in Game 2 hero Didier Fuentes to face Max Muncy.
Fuentes got Muncy to ground out, Hernandez moving to second, but he walked pinch-hitter Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases with two outs.
Weiss had a quick hook, pulling Fuentes and handing the ball to veteran Robert Suarez to face Pages. Pages got ahead in the count, 3-and-1, then swung and missed at a 99.1 mph fastball from Suarez. He got another fastball on the full count and didn’t miss, stroking it through the middle for the Dodgers’ first – and only hit – with a runner in scoring position in their 16 at-bats in those situations during the four games of this series.
Runs had been hard to come by in Atlanta. After Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Chris Sale squared off in Game 3, Mahle and Tyler Glasnow allowed just a dirty run each through the first six innings.
In the bottom of the first, Michael Harris II led off with a single off of Glasnow. He stole second, went to third on a ground out and score when Glasnow spiked a knuckle curve in the dirt well in front of home plate. It bounced off Will Smith’s chest protector back towards the mound and Glasnow couldn’t retrieve it in time to get Harris.
In the top of the second, Shohei Ohtani took a five-pitch walk, stole second and went to third when Braves catcher Sean Murphy threw the ball into center field. Ohtani scored when Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubon dropped Max Muncy’s pop-up in shallow left field.
Mahle struck out only four in his 6⅓ innings (three of them consecutively in the fourth inning) and got just seven swings-and-misses on 95 pitches. But he got a lot of soft contact – and when he didn’t, it usually found a Braves fielder’s glove. The Dodgers hit seven balls in the first six innings with exit velocities of 95 mph or higher (the StatCast standard for “hard-hit”). Only one of them was a base hit – Pages’ third-inning single (106.7 mph).
Against Glasnow, the Braves just didn’t make much contact at all.
He gave up that leadoff single to Harris in the first inning but no other hits. He did walk five, though, including two in the fifth inning that prompted Manager Dave Roberts to pull him from the game after 78 pitches.
Dodgers pitchers somehow walked 18 batters in the series but let none of them score. Alex Vesia retired Matt Olson to end that fifth inning. Edgardo Henriquez held the Braves scoreless over the next two. Tanner Scott retired the slumping heart of the Braves’ order and Muncy gave Edwin Diaz cushion in the ninth inning with a solo home run (his 19th career postseason homer, a franchise record).
More to come on this story.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Teoscar Hernández Believes Looks at Atlanta Bullpen Will Help
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers leave Los Angeles tied 1-1 in the NLDS, but Teoscar Hernández believes the first two games may still help them as the series shifts to Atlanta. The Braves have already shown the Dodgers a lot of their bullpen, and Hernández thinks that can matter when the same arms start showing up again in Games 3 and 4. With Chris Sale waiting for them Tuesday, the Dodgers will need every edge they can get. A Better Read on Atlanta’s Bullpen “I think so,” Hernández said when asked
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers leave Los Angeles tied 1-1 in the NLDS, but Teoscar Hernández believes the first two games may still help them as the series shifts to Atlanta.
The Braves have already shown the Dodgers a lot of their bullpen, and Hernández thinks that can matter when the same arms start showing up again in Games 3 and 4. With Chris Sale waiting for them Tuesday, the Dodgers will need every edge they can get.
A Better Read on Atlanta’s Bullpen
“I think so,” Hernández said when asked whether seeing so many Atlanta relievers could help later in the series. “Moving forward, now that we’ve seen basically the best out of the bullpen, we can have a better plan. We can make a better plan for Tuesday and Wednesday.”
Atlanta leaned heavily on its bullpen in Game 2 and found a way to hold the Dodgers to one run. Hernández said the Dodgers will take what they learned from those matchups and use it when they see those pitchers again.
He also brushed aside the idea that Sunday felt like a major missed chance because of the number of pitchers Atlanta had already used during the Wild Card round.
“Not really,” he said. “We didn’t think about it. We were just trying to make the best plan that we could get for the series and trying to execute whatever we have to do.”
Experience Matters Now
With the series down to three games, Hernández pointed to the Dodgers’ recent postseason experience as something they can draw on.
“I think it’s big,” he said. “We’ve been in tougher spots than this one. It’s a one-one series.
“We all know they’re going to have the best starting pitcher that they have in Sale. We’re just going to try to be ready, go with the best plan and try to execute it.”
The Dodgers will counter Sale with Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
“It’s good,” Hernández said. “That’s the best pitcher that we have going against the best pitcher that they have. It’s going to be a good matchup, a good game.
“Hopefully at the end of the day, we get the win.”
Getting the Offense Going
The Dodgers have relied almost entirely on home runs for their scoring through the first two games, and Hernández said the answer is tied to better at-bats and strike-zone control.
“It’s just having good at-bats, not swinging at bad pitches,” he said. “Like I was saying, they were executing really good pitches today. They didn’t give us a really good chance to score runs.”
Hernández felt the Dodgers stayed patient Sunday.
“Yeah, I feel so,” he said. “Like I said, they made some good pitches, borderline pitches. It’s one of those days.”
Even with runners reaching throughout the game, Hernández said the approach in the dugout stayed the same.
“Just go in there, fight every at-bat, every pitch, and try to get a good result at the end of the day.”
The Dodgers will get another look at Atlanta’s pitching Tuesday. This time, Sale will be the first challenge. After that, Hernández believes the familiarity gained over the first two games could start working in their favor.

A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
ナ・リーグ地区シリーズ第4戦（ブレーブス－ドジャース、7日、アトランタ）米大リーグ、ドジャースのエンリケ・ヘルナンデス内野手（34）が地区シリーズ第4戦前の会見に登壇し、第3戦で先発した山本由伸投手（28）にマウンドでかけた「汚い言葉」を明かした。
第3戦の五回は山本が1死満塁のピンチを背負うと、捕手のスミスと三塁のE・ヘルナンデスが右腕に声をかけた。山本はその言葉を「すごく汚い言葉でした」と苦笑いを浮かべるも、「すごく励まされました」と明かしていた。
キケは「これはお前の試合だ。誰もブルペンで準備していない。これはお前の試合なんだ。お前を信頼している。これまでも切り抜けてきたし、今回も必ず切り抜けられると分かっている。自分にプレッシャーをかけすぎず、そのまま行け」と背中を押す言葉を投げかけたという。
さらに山本は米国の汚い言葉も知っているかという問いに「彼はアメリカ語を話すよ。アメリカ語だ」と報道陣の笑いを誘い、「これまで一緒にプレーしてきた中でも最も頭のいい選手の一人。彼は野球に対して注ぐのと同じくらいの努力と熱意を、英語の勉強にも注いでいる。試合の前にも後にも英語の授業を受けている。誰も見ていないところでも、家に帰って英語のレッスンを受けている。今ではほとんど普通に会話できる。時にはGoogle翻訳が必要になることもあるが、ちゃんと会話が成立するよ」と影の努力まで明かした。

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers star Mookie Betts' birthday feat making MLB history proves he's a true champion appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
On Wednesday evening, the Los Angeles Dodgers will look to turn out the lights on the Atlanta Braves when the two teams hit the field for Game 4 of their NLDS matchup. The Dodgers climbed back into the driver's seat in this series on Tuesday in a Game 3 win thanks to an epic performance from pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
It's been a relatively quiet postseason thus far for Dodgers leadoff hitter Mookie Betts, but perhaps a personal milestone on Wednesday could help change that.
"Today is Mookie Betts' birthday. Birthdays are important. This will be the fourth time he plays a postseason game on his birthday, most in MLB history," reported Sarah Langs of the MLB on X, formerly Twitter.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Indeed, having a birthday in October means that Betts is no stranger to playing postseason baseball on the special occasion. He turns 34 years old on Wednesday, and has looked like an aging star for most of the series so far against the Braves, not making much happen at the plate.
However, on Wednesday, the Dodgers found a way to get to Braves ace Chris Sale thanks to two straight homers, the second of which was launched by former Atlanta star Freddie Freeman, to put three runs on the board, which was all they needed to get the comfortable win.
The Dodgers now sit just one win away from the NLCS, where they would play either the San Diego Padres or Milwaukee Brewers for the right to go to the World Series.
In any case, Game 4 of Braves vs Dodgers is set to get underway on Wednesday at 6:00 pm ET from Atlanta.
Related: Dodgers' Miguel Rojas not available for Game 4 of NLDS vs. Braves

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Kiké Hernández Makes Incredible MLB History Thanks to Postseason Success
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: It's October, so of course Dodgers utility man Kiké Hernández is making an impact. item.content:encoded:
It's October, so of course Dodgers utility man Kiké Hernández is making an impact.
On Tuesday, the Dodgers took back home-field advantage and secured a 2-1 series lead over the Atlanta Braves with their 3-1 win. They are one win away from their third consecutive National League Championship Series appearance and fifth in the last seven seasons.
Hernández's play once again helped the Dodgers to a victory in October, and in the process, he made MLB history.
According to OptaSTATS, Hernández is the only player in MLB history to have at least 10% of his career home runs (regular season and postseason) come in the postseason (minimum 100 total homers).
The 35-year-old is currently at 11.3% (17-out-of-151). OptaSTATS said that the next closest is Houston Astros' Jose Altuve at 9.4%.
The veteran Dodger transforms into a stud once the calendar flips to October. He goes from a steady utility player in the regular season into a postseason monster, boosting his career OPS from .706 up to .831.
“It’s something I take a lot of pride in, but don’t think about it too much,” Hernández said after the game. “Once I’m done playing, I’m going to be someone that looks back and be really proud of my career because of how my career has gone in terms of finding myself each and every year in October.”
Kiké Hernández Takes His Game to Another Level in October
In the past, the longtime Dodger has noted that the intensity and stakes of the postseason sharply elevate his focus and adrenaline compared to the grind of a 162-game regular season.
In 105 postseason games, the Puerto Rican native has hit .272 with a .831 OPS, 17 home runs, 44 RBIs and 81 hits in 298 at-bats.
The Dodgers have scored 10 runs through three games in the NLDS, all of which have come via the long ball. That is the longest streak to start a postseason in MLB history.
Hernández's home run in the fourth inning broke a scoreless tie. It was a two-run shot to left field with Andy Pages on base.
"He's a big-time player," manager Dave Roberts said after the game. "I said earlier, we needed a little bit of that Kiké dust. And he's always prepared. And he loves moments like this. He has a way to lock in. ... It's just one of those things that having him in a lineup in the postseason just adds that extra sort of urgency, that kind of grit that you need."
Two batters later, Freddie Freeman hit a solo shot to right-center against his former team to extend the lead to 3-0.
That was more then enough for ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was on it on Tuesday night.
The 28-year-old pitched seven great innings, allowing just one run on four hits with 10 strikeouts across 98 pitches.
Yamamoto is 33-0 (including the postseason) when he gets at least three runs of support.
The Dodgers will look to close out the series on Wednesday, with first pitch is at 3 p.m. PT.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Kiké Hernández, in yet another stroke of postseason magic, delivered when the team needed him the most. Kike Hernandez’s moment After the Dodgers struggled offensively in Game 2, and with a lefty on the mound — an all-world pitcher nonetheless, like Chris Sale — manager Dave Roberts turned to Hernandez to start in Game 3 of the NLDS. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Kiké Hernández, in yet another stroke of postseason magic, delivered when the team needed him the most.
Kike Hernandez’s moment
After the Dodgers struggled offensively in Game 2, and with a lefty on the mound — an all-world pitcher nonetheless, like Chris Sale — manager Dave Roberts turned to Hernandez to start in Game 3 of the NLDS.
Despite not featuring much during the regular season and producing little when he did, Hernandez hit a two-run home run against Sale.
It opened the scoring for the Dodgers and gave Yoshinobu Yamamoto a cushion. Those two runs would have been enough, with Freddie Freeman’s solo shot serving as insurance.
For Hernandez to deliver once again, now 35 years old, it really does show that there is something about high-stakes moments that bring out the best in Hernandez.
“He’s a big-time player,” Roberts said. “We needed a little bit of that Kiké dust. He’s always prepared and he loves moments like this. … Having him in the lineup in the postseason just adds that extra sort of urgency, that kind of grit that you need.”
How Kike Hernandez always delivers in the postseason
Freeman, who has seen and done a lot in baseball, celebrated how ready Hernandez stays for these kinds of moments.
“I wish there was a recipe for that so we can all take it from him,” Freeman said.
“He’s incredible. He shows up when you need him. He hasn’t had a start in a while, and he goes out there and does what he did. … He’s a Swiss Army knife, and he’s ready to go at all times.”
Hernandez’s home run was the 17th of his postseason career. In fact, he is now the only player in MLB history to have at least 10.0% of his career homers come in the postseason, with at least 100 career home runs.
“That’s probably something that, once I’m done playing, I’m going to look back and be really proud of my career because of how I find myself each and every year in October,” he said.
Until he is done, the Dodgers may need to count on Hernandez one more time, and he will keep himself ready.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers Manager Dave Roberts Raves About 'Big-Time Player' Kiké Hernández
Kiké Hernández only has one hit in the 2026 MLB playoffs, but it's the biggest hit of the year for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
With Game 3 of the National League Division Series scoreless in the top of the fourth inning and a runner on first base with nobody out, Hernández crushed a changeup from Atlanta Braves ace Chris Sale over the left field wall for a two-run home run, giving the Dodgers a 2-0 lead. Ultimately, that long ball would be enough for Los Angeles to get a 3-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves and take a 2-1 series lead.
"He's a big-time player," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Hernández in his postgame press conference on Tuesday night. "I said it earlier, we needed a little bit of that Kiké dust, and he's always prepared, and he loves moments like this. He has a way to lock in. He doubled up on a changeup, and he put a good swing on it and made a couple really nice defensive plays, as well.
"It's just one of those things where having him in a lineup in the postseason just adds that extra sort of urgency and that kind of grit that you need."
The aforementioned home run was the 12th postseason long ball for Hernández in a Dodgers uniform; Hernández, who has extensive experience at every position but catcher (he has even made 11 appearances on the mound), is in his second stint and 10th overall season with the Dodgers (2015-20 and 2023-present).
Two batters after Hernández went deep, first baseman Freddie Freeman did the same, launching a solo home run to right. On the hill, Los Angeles got seven potent innings from right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who logged 10 strikeouts and gave up just one run and five baserunners (four hits and one walk). Tanner Scott and Edwin Díaz followed with a scoreless inning of relief apiece.
The 35-year-old Hernández, who traditionally gets lauded for his defensive play and versatility, has been a postseason hero for the Dodgers. With Los Angeles trailing the Toronto Blue Jays 3-2 in the 2025 World Series and trying to extend the series, Hernández turned a game-ending double-play in left field with the tying run in scoring position to force Game 7, which the Dodgers would win in 11 innings.
In 2020, Hernández hit a game-tying home run in the bottom of the sixth inning against the Braves in Game 7 of the NLCS, which the Dodgers went on to win, and he drove in one of the Dodgers' two runs against the San Diego Padres in Game 5 of the 2024 NLDS on a solo home run.
Meanwhile, Hernández blasted three home runs for the Dodgers in a closeout Game 5 victory over the Chicago Cubs in the 2017 NLCS and hit five home runs across 11 postseason games for the Boston Red Sox in 2021.
Hernández, who started at third base for the Dodgers in Game 3 and later moved to left field, was limited to 41 games in the 2026 regular season due to elbow and oblique injuries, respectively.
In all, the Dodgers have scored just 10 runs in the NLDS, but they've held the Braves to seven runs. The Dodgers have the chance to advance to the NL Championship Series in Game 4 on Wednesday afternoon (6 p.m. ET on FS1). Atlanta will send Tyler Mahle to the hill, while Los Angeles counters with Tyler Glasnow.
Should the Dodgers advance, they'd play the winner of the NLDS matchup between the Milwaukee Brewers and Padres, who staved off elimination with a Game 3 win on Tuesday night, in the NLCS.

item.title: [El Nuevo Día] ¡Boricuas brillan en octubre! Kike Hernández jonronea y Edwin Díaz salva juego en Atlanta
item.dc:creator: Charles Odum

item.content:encoded:
7 de octubre de 2026 - 9:45 PM
Atlanta - Yoshinobu Yamamoto ponchó a 10 bateadores en siete entradas, Enrique “Kike” Hernández conectó un jonrón de dos carreras y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 3-1 a los Braves de Atlanta el martes por la noche, tomando una ventaja de 2-1 en su Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Hernández, quien suele brillar en octubre, sacudió su decimoséptimo cuadrangular en postemporada, quebrando un empate con el miembro del Salón de la Fama de Béisbol Carlos Beltrán.
El boricua ahora está empate con Jim Thome, Aaron Judge y David Ortiz en la lista de jonrones en la postemporada.
Yamamoto dominó el muy esperado duelo contra el as de Atlanta, Chris Sale, quien permitió tres carreras y siete imparables en cinco entradas. Yamamoto, Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Serie Mundial de 2025, concedió solo cuatro hits y una base por bolas, mejorando su récord de postemporada a 8-1.
Los Dodgers pueden ganar la serie —pactada al mejor de cinco juegos— y dar un paso más en su intento de convertirse en el primer equipo de la Liga Nacional en ganar tres títulos consecutivos de Serie Mundial si vencen nuevamente a los Braves el miércoles por la noche en el cuarto partido.
Los Braves esperaban que dar descanso adicional a Sale fuera una fórmula ganadora para este crucial tercer encuentro. Sin embargo, tras dejar a seis corredores en base en las primeras tres entradas, permitió el jonrón de dos carreras de Hernández y un cuadrangular solitario de Freddie Freeman en el cuarto episodio.
Ozzie Albies abrió la novena entrada de Atlanta con un doblete contra el muro entre el jardín derecho y el central ante los lanzamientos de Edwin Díaz, avanzando a tercera base tras un rodado de out de Michael Harris II. Díaz dejó al corredor varado cuando Mauricio Dubón fue puesto out en un elevado de foul al jardín derecho y Mike Yastrzemski fue retirado con un rodado al campocorto Mookie Betts.
Tras una temporada agobiado por lesiones, Díaz se apuntó su primer salvado desde el pasado 14 de agosto, cuando lanzó la novena entrada en blanco contra Milwaukee.
FUe además su primer rescate de postemporada desde el 14 de octubre de 2024, cuanto se apuntó un salvamento por los Mets de Nueva York contra los propios Dodgers en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional.
Dubón realizó una atrapada saltando sobre la barda del jardín izquierdo para robarle un jonrón a Freeman en la tercera entrada; sin embargo, Freeman logró conectar su cuadrangular una entrada más tarde. El jonrón de Hernández hacia el jardín izquierdo impulsó a Andy Pages, quien había conectado un sencillo. Un out después, Freeman conectó el jonrón número 18 de su carrera en postemporada hacia el jardín derecho, ampliando la ventaja a 3-0.
El mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, bajó al bateador designado Shohei Ohtani al quinto puesto del orden al bate, debido a que Ohtani registraba un promedio de 3 de 15 en su carrera contra Sale. Ohtani se había ido de 4-0 con dos ponches ante Sale cuando los Dodgers perdieron 1-0 el 26 de agosto en Atlanta. Roberts predijo acertadamente que Ohtani tendría oportunidades con corredores en base al batear en una posición más baja del orden de bateo.
En la primera entrada, con corredores en primera y segunda, Sale ponchó a Ohtani para cerrar el episodio. En la tercera, con dos corredores en base, Ohtani llegó a primera gracias a una interferencia del receptor Drake Baldwin —lo que llenó las bases—, antes de que Miguel Rojas terminara la entrada con un elevado al jardín derecho. Ohtani recibió una base por bolas al abrir la octava entrada frente a Brent Suter, el cuarto lanzador de Atlanta.
Un rodado de Baldwin a primera base, con las bases llenas, impulsó a Dubón —quien había conectado un sencillo— en la quinta entrada, anotando así la única carrera de Atlanta ante Yamamoto.
Rojas abandonó el partido durante un turno al bate en la octava entrada. El segunda base pareció lastimarse la espalda al realizar un swing y fue sustituido por Tommy Edman. Los Dodgers informaron que la lesión consistía en dolor en la zona lumbar.
Tanner Scott sumó dos ponches en una octava entrada sin anotaciones para Los Ángeles.
Las noticias explicadas de forma sencilla y directa para entender lo más importante del día.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers SP Yoshinobu Yamamoto Makes MLB History in NLDS Win
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Prendergrast
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are one win away from reaching the National League Championship Series for the third consecutive year. The Dodgers entered Game 3 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves needing a crucial win to take a 2-1 series lead. That is why they called on Yoshinobu Yamamoto to start the game. Yamamoto has been a big-game pitcher throughout his career, and he won the World Series MVP last season. The Dodgers started Yamamoto on the road for Game 3 against the Braves' ace Chris Sale.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are one win away from reaching the National League Championship Series for the third consecutive year.
The Dodgers entered Game 3 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves needing a crucial win to take a 2-1 series lead. That is why they called on Yoshinobu Yamamoto to start the game. Yamamoto has been a big-game pitcher throughout his career, and he won the World Series MVP last season.
The Dodgers started Yamamoto on the road for Game 3 against the Braves' ace Chris Sale. Yamamoto got the better of that matchup, throwing 7.0 innings, allowing only four hits and one run, and striking out 10.
The righty earned his first postseason win and set an historic record. According to OptaSTATS, Yamamoto is the only pitcher in MLB history to earn a win in five straight postseason appearances without allowing more than one run or one walk. Each of those wins has been on the road.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto is the only pitcher in MLB history to earn the win in 5 straight postseason appearances while not allowing more than 1 run or 1 walk in any of them.
All 5 have come on the road. https://t.co/QwWmubt7fS
— OptaSTATS (@OptaSTATS) October 7, 2026
It is hard to find a more dominant postseason pitcher in baseball than Yamamoto. He has been rock solid for a Dodgers pitching staff that has been often injured over the years.
Yamamoto's Postseason Prowess
What Yamamoto did last season is hard to replicate. In the 2025 World Series, Yamamoto threw 17.2 innings, allowed only 10 hits and two runs, and won three games, including Games 6 and 7.
His first playoff start this season picked up right where he left off. He will likely be a workhorse for the Dodgers again this postseason as they go for the elusive three-peat, which has only been done a few times in sports.
The next time we will likely see Yamamoto is in the NLCS if the Dodgers make it. However, if their season comes down to a Game 5 in the NLDS, we know Yamamoto will be available.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Dodgers SP Yoshinobu Yamamoto Makes MLB History in NLDS Win appeared first on HEAVY.

1勝1敗で迎えた第3戦は、ブレーブスの左腕クリス・セールとの投げ合いとなった。山本はポストシーズンで自身最多となる10三振を奪い、相手打線を封じた。
打線は四回、エンリケ・ヘルナンデスの2ランとフレディ・フリーマンのソロで3点を先取。山本は五回に1点を失ったものの、七回まで追加点を許さず、リードを救援陣につないだ。
八回はタナー・スコット、九回はエドウィン・ディアスが無失点に抑えた。投打がかみ合ったドジャースは、先に3勝したチームが勝ち上がる地区シリーズで、突破まであと1勝に迫った。
まるスポ編集部

item.title: [WSLS] Yamamoto is dominant again as Dodgers ride homers from Hernández and Freeman to 3-1 win over Braves
item.dc:creator: Charles Odum; Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA – Yoshinobu Yamamoto felt trust from Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts when he remained in a crucial NL Division Series game after a stressful fifth inning. “I’d like to continue living up to the highest expectation,” Yamamoto said through a translator. Recommended Videos The right-hander from Japan continues to do more than just meet expectations in the postseason. Yamamoto struck out 10 in seven brilliant innings, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and the Dodgers beat the Atlan
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA – Yoshinobu Yamamoto felt trust from Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts when he remained in a crucial NL Division Series game after a stressful fifth inning.
“I’d like to continue living up to the highest expectation,” Yamamoto said through a translator.
Recommended Videos
The right-hander from Japan continues to do more than just meet expectations in the postseason.
Yamamoto struck out 10 in seven brilliant innings, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and the Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday night to take a 2-1 lead in their NL Division Series.
Yamamoto dominated his much-anticipated matchup with Atlanta ace Chris Sale, who allowed three runs and seven hits in five innings. Last year's World Series MVP permitted only four hits and one walk while improving to 8-1 with a 2.14 ERA in 11 career postseason outings, including 10 starts.
His 10 strikeouts were a postseason high for him.
“I was confident and able to control all my pitches today,” Yamamoto said.
The Dodgers can clinch the best-of-five series and take another step toward becoming the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series by beating the Braves again Wednesday night in Game 4.
Atlanta hoped giving Sale extra rest would be a winning formula in the pivotal third game. Instead, after stranding six runners in the first three innings, he gave up the two-run homer to Hernández and a solo shot to former Braves star Freddie Freeman in the fourth.
“He was still touching 100 (mph),” manager Walt Weiss said of Sale. “The stuff was fine. Like I said, maybe the command not perfect. It wasn’t bad. But they did a nice job against him.”
That was all the offensive support Yamamoto and relievers Tanner Scott and Edwin Díaz would need.
Ozzie Albies opened the Atlanta ninth with a double off the right-center wall against Díaz and moved to third on Michael Harris II's groundout. Díaz stranded the runner and earned a save when Mauricio Dubón fouled out to right field and Mike Yastrzemski grounded out to shortstop Mookie Betts.
A homer for the boo birds
Freeman said he didn't mind being booed by Atlanta fans in the sellout crowd of 42,420.
“I’ve got a gray uniform on,” Freeman said. “I expect boos. It’s OK. ... It’s all love. I still love everybody here and I’m looking forward to tomorrow.”
Dubón made a leaping catch over the left-field wall to rob Freeman of a home run in the third. Freeman wouldn't be denied an inning later. Hernández's homer to left drove in Andy Pages, who singled. One out later, Freeman pulled his 18th career postseason homer to right field for a 3-0 lead.
Lineup change
Roberts moved designated hitter Shohei Ohtani down to No. 5 in the lineup because Ohtani was 3 for 15 in his career against Sale. Ohtani went 0 for 4 with two strikeouts against Sale when the Dodgers lost 1-0 on Aug. 26 in Atlanta.
Roberts correctly predicted Ohtani would have opportunities with runners on base hitting lower in the order.
With runners on first and second in the first, Sale struck out Ohtani to end the inning. With two runners on base in the third, Ohtani reached on catcher's interference by Drake Baldwin to load the bases before Miguel Rojas ended the inning with a flyball to right field. Ohtani walked to lead off the eighth against Brent Suter, Atlanta's fourth pitcher.
Baldwin's bases-loaded grounder to first base drove in Dubón, who singled, in the fifth for Atlanta's only run.
Injury report
Rojas left during an at-bat in the eighth. The second baseman appeared to injure his back on a swing and was replaced by Tommy Edman. The Dodgers announced the injury as lower back pain.
Roberts said Rojas probably won't start on Wednesday and his availability off the bench will be determined before the game.
“I give him credit for conceding that at-bat,” Roberts said.
Weiss made a late change, moving Ronald Acuña Jr. from right field to designated hitter. Weiss said Acuña jammed his knee on a slide in Game 2. Acuña remained in the game but the knee was sore on Tuesday, leading to the lineup change.
Milestone win for Roberts
Roberts now has 71 career postseason wins, tying Tony La Russa for second-most in major league history. Joe Torre is first with 84.
Up next
Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle is expected to face Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow in Game 4 on Wednesday night. Mahle said Tuesday an abdominal pull is now a “non-issue.” He felt the pull before allowing one run in seven innings of a 4-3 loss to Philadelphia in 10 innings during the NL Wild Card Series last week.
___

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers beat Braves on Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homers, take 2-1 NLDS lead
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article ATLANTA — The Dodgers went into Game 3 of the National League Division Series knowing they couldn’t be so reliant on the home run, especially with Braves ace Chris Sale on the mound.
