item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
ATLANTA — The Dodgers went into Game 3 of the National League Division Series knowing they couldn’t be so reliant on the home run, especially with Braves ace Chris Sale on the mound. And yet, in a 3-1 win, it was the home run ball, paired with a masterful performance on the mound from right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, that secured the victory.
The Dodgers pulled ahead to a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five series.
The Dodgers tried to score in other ways, putting on six baserunners in the first three innings of the game. But it didn’t work.
They failed to take advantage of some luck and poor defense from the Braves in the first inning, as Mookie Betts beat out a soft ground ball up the first base line and Teoscar Hernández reached on a fielding error by Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim.
Yoshinobu gives up four hits and strikes out 10 and Kiké Hernández hits a two-run home run to power the Dodgers to victory in Game 3 of the NLDS.
The lineup shuffling manager Dave Roberts did against Sale had superstar Shohei Ohtani, batting fifth, walking up to the plate with two outs and runners on first and second. His over-anxious approach at the plate so far this postseason followed him into the at-bat. And he struck out whiffing on a slider in the opposite batter’s box.
The next inning, Kyle Tucker hit a two-out single into left, baited Sale into picking over to first base twice, and then stole second. But he was stranded there, as Kiké Hernández went down swinging. All six of the Dodgers’ outs in the first two innings came via the strikeout.
In the third, the Dodgers loaded the bases. Mookie Betts started the effort with a double through the left side of the infield. And it looked for a moment as if Freddie Freeman had capitalized on the opportunity with a runner in scoring position.
He stayed back on a fastball and crushed it to deep left field, on a trajectory to just clear the short fence. But Braves left fielder Mauricio Dubón made a leaping catch, holding into the ball as he slammed into the wall.
Undeterred, the Dodgers kept putting runners on base. With two outs, Will Smith stayed through a slider to single. Ohtani clipped Braves catcher Drake Baldwin’s mitt and was awarded first base for catcher’s interference. Then Miguel Rojas, who’d exit the game in the eighth inning mid-at-bat with what the Dodgers called low back pain, hit a line drive that found leather to end the inning.
So, back to the long ball.
Perennial postseason hero Kiké Hernández delivered the first blow. With Andy Pages on first, after his first hit of the series, Hernández launched a changeup into the left-field stands. Then, two batters later, Freeman turned on an inside sinker and sent it over the right-field fence — where Dubón had no chance to track it down.
Game 3 was billed as a matchup between aces: Sale, whom the Braves tabbed for Tuesday because of his workload in their wild-card series, and Yamamoto, whom the Dodgers partially held back for the first two games with the NLCS in mind.
Yamamoto held up his end of the bargain, limiting the Braves to four hits and one run in seven innings.
He retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced. The only baserunner in that time, Michael Harris II, bunted for a single. Yamamoto crashed hard, slipping on the slick grass as he tried to pivot but still managing to make a throw to first from the ground.
Shohei Ohtani is batting fifth in the lineup against Braves ace Chris Sale in Game 3 of the NLDS. He hasn’t hit fifth or lower in a starting lineup since 2020 with the Angels.
He only wavered in the fifth, loading the bases with a pair of singles and a four-pitch walk. The Braves’ batting order turned over, and Yamamoto got Baldwin to ground out to first, but that allowed a run. Then he induced Ronald Acuña Jr. to ground out to second to escape the jam. Rojas ranged to his left to field the ball and made an on-target throw even as he slipped on the grass in shallow right field.
Yamamoto didn’t allow another baserunner.
Left-handed reliever Tanner Scott served as the Dodgers’ setup man, throwing a hitless eighth. And right-hander Edwin Díaz came in for his first save opportunity since Aug. 14 against the Brewers.
He gave up a double off the wall to Ozzie Albies to open the inning but retired the next three batters.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers World Series hero Miguel Rojas exits after experiencing discomfort

item.content:encoded:
During the eighth inning of Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, Dodgers middle infielder Miguel Rojas exited the game.
Rojas was seen in visible discomfort after fouling off a fastball from Braves reliever Brent Suter.
Rojas started limping back toward the batter’s box and was immediately evaluated by a member of the Dodgers’ training staff and manager Dave Roberts.
Shortly after the injury, the Dodgers announced that Rojas was removed from the game due to lower back pain.
Tommy Edman replaced Rojas at second base.
Rojas went 0-for-3 before departing Tuesday. He has one hit in the series — a double in Saturday’s 5-3 victory.
Rojas is expected to retire after the season is over.
Rojas was a World Series hero last year after hitting a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Blue Jays, sending the game to extra innings.
The Dodgers went on to win the game in the 11th when Will Smith hit a go-ahead home run.
In Tuesday’s game, the Dodgers’ offense popped off in the fourth inning, when Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homered to give LA a 3-0 lead.
The Braves scored in the fifth when Drake Baldwin grounded out to first after Dodgers starting pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto loaded the bases.
Yamamoto finished with a career-high 10 strikeouts. He tossed 98 pitches in seven innings, giving up four hits, one run and one walk.

item.content:encoded:
In a game that could have a massive shift in momentum in either direction for both teams, the Atlanta Braves bring future HOFer Chris Sale to the mound amidst one of the best seasons of his career against Yoshinobu Yamamoto during the best season of his young career.
The last time these two pitchers faced off the Braves beat the Dodgers 1-0 when Chris Sale pitched a complete game shutout on August twenty-seventh. A repeat of that exact result is slim, but if Sale could pitch a long game today, it would be welcomed among the bullpen that has already had back-to-back games where they carried the load.
Drake Baldwin was the offensive hero the last time the Braves faced Yamamoto with a solo shot that was the only run of the game.
First pitch is at 6:00 pm EDT. Follow along in the comments.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Los Angeles Dodgers Make Sudden Freddie Freeman Move Before Braves Game

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are tied with the Atlanta Braves at one game apiece in their best-of-five series in the NLDS.
On Tuesday night, the two teams will meet for Game 3 at Truist Park in Atlanta, with the Braves sending out left-handed ace Chris Sale while L.A. will start right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto in what should be one of the best pitching matchups we’ve seen so far this postseason.
Ahead of the game, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made some major lineup changes, including one involving veteran slugger Freddie Freeman.
Dodgers Announce Freeman Move
With Shohei Ohtani struggling at the plate recently, Roberts decided to move him down to the No. 5 spot in the lineup Tuesday night.
As a result, Freeman will move up from the cleanup spot to the No. 2 spot, while Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot.
Teoscar Hernandez and Will Smith will fill the No. 3 and No. 4 spots, while the back end of the order will remain fairly close to what the Dodgers have used recently, despite bringing Andy Pages back into the lineup.
Here’s the full Dodgers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Dodgers 10/6 M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF W. Smith C S. Ohtani DH M. Rojas 2B A. Pages CF K. Tucker RF E. Hernández 3B Y. Yamamoto SP.”
Dodgers 10/6
M. Betts SS
F. Freeman 1B
T. Hernández LF
W. Smith C
S. Ohtani DH
M. Rojas 2B
A. Pages CF
K. Tucker RF
E. Hernández 3B
Y. Yamamoto SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) October 6, 2026
Freeman’s 2026 Postseason
While it’s only been two games, Freeman has been one of the most consistent bats in the Dodgers’ lineup against his former team.
He’s recorded three hits across seven at-bats, including two on Sunday, one of which was a home run.
Freeman spent the first 12 years of his MLB career with the Braves and became one of the greatest players in franchise history. Now, he’ll play the next two games in a ballpark he called home for more than a decade.

item.title: [ABC7 Los Angeles] Dodgers land two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal in blockbuster deadline deal, sources say
item.dc:creator: Alden Gonzalez

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- For as much as they might have downplayed the possibility behind closed doors, the Los Angeles Dodgers were long seen by rival executives as overwhelming favorites to land generational ace Tarik Skubal. Their farm system was too good, their goals were too lofty, their rotation had become too uncertain.
On Saturday night, a day and a half before the trade deadline, they pulled it off.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal, the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner, from the Detroit Tigers for a package of three prospects: outfielder Zhyir Hope, and right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Skubal, a 29-year-old pending free agent, will now headline what was arguably already the best rotation in the sport. Alongside him will be Yoshinobu Yamamoto, making a strong case for a Cy Young of his own, followed by Blake Snell, Shohei Ohtani and Tyler Glasnow, all of whom are in varying stages of returning from injury.
The Dodgers had long touted their depth as a reason they didn't necessarily need Skubal. Snell, who has made one start all year, is expected to rejoin the rotation after his next rehab outing. Glasnow, out since May 6 with back spasms, will begin a minor league rehab assignment next week. And though Ohtani is still troubled by a sore left knee that only seems to bother him on the mound, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said earlier this week he fully expects him to pitch in October.
The Game 1 starter, though, will be Skubal, who might be the best pitcher in the world.
Skubal boasts a 2.79 ERA in 16 starts this year, striking out 116 batters and issuing 14 walks in 96 innings. The only thing that could stop him were bone chips that began to cause irritation in his left elbow in late April. Skubal underwent a less-invasive, revolutionary NanoScope procedure and returned in about six weeks. His ERA in July is 2.03. And as he addressed the media in the visiting clubhouse at Sutter Health Park in Sacramento late Saturday night, moments after being informed of the trade, Skubal at one point got choked up.
"Going into the season, this isn't what I planned on doing," Skubal said before getting on the verge of tears while reflecting on his time in Detroit. "But circumstances change, situations change. I'm very appreciative of everything that the Tigers have done for me."
A late bloomer who lasted until the ninth round of the 2018 draft, Skubal began to emerge as one of the game's most talented pitchers in 2022 and 2023 and took it to another level thereafter. From 2024 to 2025, Skubal went 31-10 with a 2.30 ERA and a whopping 469 strikeouts in 387 innings. His 12.6 FanGraphs wins above replacement led all major league pitchers.
When Skubal and members of the Tigers' front office exchanged arbitration figures in the ensuing offseason, the two sides were $13 million apart. An independent arbitrator ruled in favor of Skubal and his agent, Scott Boras, rewarding him a $32 million salary as he headed into his free-agent year.
Rumors had swirled throughout the offseason that the Tigers would trade him then. Instead, they doubled down, signing fellow starter Framber Valdez to a three-year, $115 million contract with the hope of winning the AL Central. Instead, the Tigers flopped. By the end of May, they were tied with the Colorado Rockies for the worst record in the majors, prompting executives throughout the industry to assume Skubal would be traded.
The Tigers proceeded to win 28 of their next 46 games, and suddenly it seemed as if Skubal might stay. But their momentum ran out. The Tigers lost back-to-back games to the last-place Kansas City Royals over the weekend and dropped two of three to the Baltimore Orioles thereafter. The last of those losses, on Wednesday night, saw Skubal take the mound and record his 1,000th career strikeout, then sit in the dugout while his team blew a 7-0 lead.
After it was over, the Tigers were seven games below .500, six games out of first place and three games out of a wild-card spot.
To many observing Skubal's availability, it was a death knell to his time in Detroit.
The Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers, New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays were all in on Skubal to some extent, with the Brewers, deep in prospects, the favorites among that group. But the Dodgers were the clear frontrunners all along. And now they'll add Skubal to a laundry list of talent they've acquired from the outside over the years, following Ohtani, Snell, Yamamoto, Glasnow, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and, this offseason, Edwin Diaz and Kyle Tucker.
The vast majority of those players came via free agency. The Dodgers loathe the high asking prices at midseason. But in getting Skubal, they parted from an outfield group that is stocked with talent -- one that is still headlined by Josue DePaula, a consensus top-25 prospect, along with Eduardo Quintero, ranked 45th on Kiley McDaniel's latest ESPN rankings. They also maintain all of their young major league starting pitching, namely Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan and Roki Sasaki.
In Hope and Ryan, though, the Tigers came away with two top-50 prospects.
Hope, 21, was slashing .293/.369/.530 with 23 home runs and 18 stolen bases for the Dodgers' Double-A affiliate and brings explosive power from the left side, top-tier speed and an ability to handle center field.
Ryan, 27, made a brief stint in the major leagues in 2024, putting up a 1.33 ERA in four starts. He then underwent a prolonged rehab from Tommy John surgery and has made eight starts in Triple-A, putting up a 4.46 ERA. He has been out since the middle of June with a hamstring injury, but McDaniel ranked him 49th in his midseason top 50 in May.
Smith, 21, was a third-round pick out of high school in 2023 who has put up a 3.88 ERA in 19 starts at the Class A level this season.
In three months, Skubal will head into the open market with the chance of signing the most lucrative deal ever rewarded to a starting pitcher. Before then, he will join a Dodgers club that boasts the highest run-differential and second-best record in the major leagues -- and help them try to become the first team in NL history to win three consecutive championships.
Asked his thoughts about joining the Dodgers, Skubal took about 15 seconds to compose himself before saying: "Yeah, it's exciting. I'm excited. They've got a good group."

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Blake Snell’s rocky outing leads to de facto bullpen game
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers needed one win to send the Atlanta Braves to the brink of elimination on Sunday. Instead, the Braves lineup forced an early exit from Blake Snell and scored two defining runs against the bullpen in a 3-2 win over the Dodgers, forcing the series back to Atlanta for Games 3 and 4.
It wasn't the first rocky outing for Snell against Atlanta this season, as he only managed to toss three innings while allowing four runs in his 2026 debut back on May 8 before being placed on the injured list. The southpaw had looked like his usual dominant stretch once he returned in August, but the ultimate test was to see how he would perform against the lone team that roughed him up.
Snell made quick work of Drake Baldwin for the first out, but after allowing a one-out single to Ronald Acuña Jr., he walked both Matt Olson and Ozzie Albies to load the bases. Snell managed to get Michael Harris II to fly out in foul territory for a crucial second out, but Mauricio Dubón tacked on the game's first run with an infield single. Snell faced seven hitters in the first inning, needing 27 pitches to give the Dodgers a chance to hit.
Snell's biggest flaw on Sunday was his inability to get quick innings, unlike Tarik Skubal on Saturday. Snell needed four pitches to get two quick outs in the second inning, but allowed a six-pitch walk to Baldwin and needed another eight to strike out Acuña. Snell allowed another two-out baserunner in the third inning, this time a single from Harris, needing 19 pitches after tossing 18 the inning prior.
Snell's hopes at a clean inning were dashed in the fourth inning, as he walked a pair of hitters and tossed 26 pitches before the plug was pulled on his night. The Dodgers got him off the hook in the bottom of the fourth inning with a Freddie Freeman home run, but the Dodgers employed six relievers out of the bullpen over their final 5 1/3 innings on the mound.
Snell had a postseason to remember last year, as his defining moment came in Game 1 of the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers, facing the minimum over eight shutout innings. Sunday's outing was the first time he failed to log four innings in a postseason start since he began the 2022 Wild Card series against the New York Mets back when he was a San Diego Padre. Out of the 90 pitches he tossed against Atlanta, 47 of them went for strikes.
Snell's final start of the regular season was limited to just one inning after he dealt with left groin inflammation. Dave Roberts was quick to deny any concern over Snell's groin issue, noting that he was battling himself on the mound.
"No, it wasn't that. He was fighting himself in his delivery all game. Today, I just think the fastball was really good, the changeup was good at times, but I think, in total, didn't have fastball command, didn't have slider command, and the changeup wasn't there. He was pulling it. I think overall it wasn't the groin, and he wasn't sharp tonight."
Roberts felt optimistic about his chances of Snell on the mound while Atlanta went with their own bullpen game, beginning with left-hander Ray Kerr. The pieces just couldn't fall into place on Sunday.
"Felt great. Anytime I feel I have Blake Snell lined up against any pitcher felt good. Going to getting Kerr out of the game and then getting [Grant] Holmes out of the game, I felt really good where we were at. I really did. We just couldn't execute as the game progressed."
Now the Dodgers will face the only pitcher to shut them out in the regular season, left-hander Chris Sale, in a crucial Game 3 at Truist Park on Tuesday. Yoshinobu Yamamoto will take the mound for the first time in the playoffs since his Herculean performance in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series.

item.content:encoded:
After the Atlanta Braves captured a 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS Game Two on Sunday afternoon, the series between the two World Series hopefuls is knotted at one apiece, with the series shifting to Atlanta for the next two games.
LA outhomered the Braves 2-0 in Game Two, and all of the Dodgers’ runs have come via the homer, which is a bit concerning. Dodgers’ infielder Freddie Freeman hit a solo shot on Sunday evening, but ultimately, LA came up short.
Following the game, Freeman spoke with the media and shared his reaction to the loss, as well as his thoughts on how the series is going thus far.
Freddie Freeman Shares Thoughts on Dodgers Loss to Braves
Via SportsNetLA, here is what Freddie Freeman had to say after the Dodgers’ loss on Sunday:
“Gotta find a way to score some runs without hitting a home run; that’s our biggest thing right now.”
“Two really good teams going at it,” Freeman also noted.
Freddie has emerged as a true leader on the Dodgers roster, and he makes a great point. LA was 0-for-8 with runners in scoring position on Sunday, so they had no issue tallying baserunners, but driving them in was the issue.
NLDS Between Dodgers and Braves Shifting to LA
The Dodgers got a solid outing from Blake Snell on Sunday, but walks were a huge issue; despite the Braves going to a bullpen game, Didier Fuentes shut down the Dodgers offense from the 6th inning on.
However, now both teams will have their ace starters going on Tuesday, with Atlanta opting to start Chris Sale, and LA going with Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
Game Three is the biggest game of both teams’ respective seasons, and with both All-Star starters going, it should be another tense, low-scoring affair.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers lost to the Atlanta Braves, 3-2, on Sunday as the National League Division Series evened out to one game apiece. With the best-of-five series now heading back to Atlanta, the two-time defending champions are in a much more troublesome spot than expected.
Left-hander Blake Snell was far from his best on Sunday as he struck out five across 3.2 innings of work (90 pitches) with an earned run and five walks. Snell, Kris Bubic and Edgardo Henriquez all allowed an earned run while the four remaining relievers were hitless in their respective outings.
Offensively, Freddie Freeman tied things up in the fourth inning with a solo home run, just his second since the All-Star break. When the Dodgers were down to their final out, Max Muncy slugged a solo home run — but it was too little too late for LA.
The Dodgers also officially announced that the starter for Game 3 of the NLDS will be the ace: Right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto. The reigning World Series MVP had a 2.16 ERA in his last five regular season starts and will now make his 2026 postseason debut.
Yamamoto will face off against southpaw Chris Sale for the Braves, who is working with a 2.16 ERA across 27 starts this season. So far in the postseason, Sale struck out nine across 6.1 innings in Atlanta's first wild-card game, and on one day of rest, closed out Game 3 of the wild-card round with three strikeouts across the game's final four outs.
Finally, manager Dave Roberts made a bold prediction regarding right fielder Kyle Tucker following his abysmal regular season to kick off the Dodgers chapter of his career. Tucker was hitting just .228 with 11 home runs going into September before he appeared to start to turn things around
“It’s been fun to watch Kyle build some confidence," Roberts said before the NLDS. "You can see him just freed up a little bit. He’s been working hard this whole year, and he’s been in it. And I give him a lot of credit for continuing to persevere and [I] expect the best of him to be at the end of the season.”

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal will kick off Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves on Saturday.
The Dodgers are yet to name their starters for the rest of the series, but Blake Snell and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are expected to pitch the next two games.
On Saturday morning, the Dodgers will announce their official 26-man roster for the NLDS.
On Friday, manager Dave Roberts provided a hint as to how many pitchers and position players will make up the squad.
“I do know we're going to go with 14 [position players] and 12 [pitchers], and now trying to figure out the bench bat, who are the extra players, is it going to be a pinch runner," Roberts said. "Yeah, I think that's kind of where we're at, and then finalizing the last reliever is always front of mind.”
In other news, the team at Dodgers On SI provided some expert predictions as to how the series will shake out. Atlanta had 94 regular season wins and is riding high after beating the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 3 of the wild-card round on Thursday, but the Dodgers have had five days of rest and are looking to make history this October.
Finally, superstar Shohei Ohtani broke his silence amid his recent activation from the injured list just in time to play in the final five regular season games of 2026. The four-time MVP isn't sure what is causing his nagging knee and biceps injuries, but is confident that he will manage it while he and his team do their best to collect 11 more wins.
“I haven't been able to get a good grasp of the root cause of all this," Ohtani said. "I think that process is going to happen during the offseason when I'm going to have a little bit more time to be able to address it. But as of now, it's something I'm just going to have to manage."

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Dodgers’ two-way star Shohei Ohtani called the past few days “very productive” and believes his swing is “in a better place” heading into a National League Division Series showdown against the Braves that begins Saturday.
But Ohtani won’t be fully healthy then and perhaps at any point this postseason. The left knee and right biceps ailments that compromised him throughout the summer will linger into the fall, Ohtani and Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Friday.
“As of now, it’s something I’m just going to have to manage,” Ohtani said through an interpreter.
Knee and biceps injuries finally sent Ohtani to the injured list in early September after a 14-game stretch during which he compiled seven hits and 22 strikeouts. Ohtani returned with five regular-season games left and was inconsistent, putting together an encouraging stretch against the San Diego Padres and an overwhelming one against the San Francisco Giants.
Ohtani took batting practice on the field during workouts Tuesday and Wednesday, a rarity for him, and Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates said those sessions were “as good as we’ve seen it this year as far as the way the ball was coming off and the way he was getting his move off.”
Bates provided some proof of that.
“He did hit a couple balls up off the scoreboard,” he said.
Ohtani also had three plate appearances against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in a prolonged simulated game Wednesday, worked out inside Thursday and came onto the field for three rounds of outdoor batting practice around 6 p.m. PT Friday. Moments later, he had two at-bats against right-hander Emmet Sheehan, striking out before hitting a line drive to right field.
“Shohei’s not 100%, but he’s going to be in the lineup,” Roberts said, adding that veteran first baseman Freddie Freeman also isn’t fully healthy, among others. “I think that most players that are performing now are not 100%. Obviously with Shohei, it’s a bigger deal because of the player, but there’s a lot of players that are not 100%, and they’ve just got to manage it.”
Despite being compromised for much of the past three months, Ohtani finished the year batting .275/.377/.512 with 30 home runs and 11 stolen bases and is likely to finish second to Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong in NL MVP voting. Ohtani also went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts, but he didn’t pitch after July 3 and had essentially been ruled out of pitching by Labor Day. Ohtani went on the IL thereafter.
“During the IL, I pretty much knew I wasn’t going to pitch the rest of the season,” Ohtani said. “So I did focus on just the hitting aspect of the game and coming to understanding and wanting to execute and try new things when I came back. So those were the things that I really took the IL time to think through what I wanted to try when I was back in action.”
Ohtani had several hard-hit balls upon returning from the injured list, notably an opposite-field double off a 103 mph fastball from star Padres closer Mason Miller. But Ohtani ultimately went 5-for-21 with eight strikeouts in his last five regular-season games, and by the end, Roberts noticed him being overanxious, trying too hard to get acclimated to major league pitching with limited time.
The 32-year-old Ohtani said he still has to make “little tweaks here and there” with his swing before feeling ready for Game 1.
He downplayed having limited playing time before then.
“Whether I have a lot of at-bats or not, I can figure out how I feel, especially in my setup,” Ohtani said. “So that’s something I was able to kind of see. But I do want to get into the postseason, feel the atmosphere and again kind of recalibrate what I have to.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — With less than 24 hours before the first pitch of Game 1 of the NLDS, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made his decision: Tarik Skubal will take the ball Saturday afternoon against the Braves.
The choice came from a rotation that gives the Dodgers perhaps as much depth as any team could ask for. Skubal earned the assignment over reigning World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, fellow two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell and All-Star right-hander Tyler Glasnow.
“With the four guys, it doesn't really matter who, but I think that we feel good about Tarik taking the baseball tomorrow afternoon,” Roberts said.
As it turns out, Skubal knew his assignment before the regular season was even over.
When Roberts pulled him after just 75 pitches in his final start in San Francisco, Skubal initially wondered why. He approached his manager, expecting there might be another reason for the early exit.
Instead, Roberts gave him a message that changed the rest of his week.
“He came and shook my hand. I was at kind of a low pitch count, I thought in the moment I was going to be able to finish the game. And he was like, ‘Get ready for Game 1,’” Skubal said.
Skubal said he was “obviously excited and fired up and ready to go.”
Now comes a new experience for the reigning back-to-back unanimous Cy Young winner.
For everything Skubal has accomplished, he has never had the opportunity to pitch at home in October. That changes Saturday, when he takes the mound in front of a Dodgers crowd for the opening game of the NLDS.
“I’m excited for the opportunity to throw in front of the fans,” Skubal said.
The left-hander also knows exactly what the atmosphere can feel like when he pitched for the Tigers.
“Usually when I walk out onto the field in a playoff game, it's usually received with a lot of boos,” Skubal said. “So I'm excited to get some cheers in there for us. And to pitch at home, I think it's going to be a ton of fun in front of this atmosphere.”
His approach for the biggest start of his Dodgers career?
Keep it simple.
“I have to be really good at what makes me good,” Skubal said.
The weather will provide another challenge, with triple-digit temperatures expected Saturday. Skubal, however, doesn't appear particularly concerned.
“We probably won't have to go to the bathroom. Just sweat it out,” he joked.
The extra time between starts has also been welcomed by the left-hander.
“I think for a starter, it's easiest to take time off,” Skubal said.
He also credited Dodgers fans for the reception he has received since arriving in Los Angeles and said he is looking forward to finally pitching in front of them in October.
“I’m excited to throw in front of them tomorrow.”
Ohtani Says His Swing Is Trending in the Right Direction
While Skubal prepares for his first postseason start at Dodger Stadium, Shohei Ohtani is preparing to return to October action after recently being activated from the 15-day injured list.
Ohtani said he feels really good overall and believes his swing has benefited from the extended break.
“I do feel like my swing is in a better place,” Ohtani said. “Just little tweaks here and there, and I’ll be ready for tomorrow.”
The time away from games, he said, has given him an opportunity to make adjustments while managing the ailments that surfaced during the second half.
“Being on the IL has taught me a lot,” Ohtani said.
But the Dodgers' star acknowledged that his lingering biceps and knee issues remain something he will have to manage throughout the postseason.
Asked whether those injuries could require attention during the offseason, Ohtani said he has not yet identified the root cause of everything he has been dealing with.
“I haven't been able to get a good grasp of the root cause of all this,” Ohtani said. “I think that process is going to happen during the off-season when I'm going to have a little bit more time to be able to address it. But as of now, it's something I'm just going to have to manage.”
That reality isn't unique to Ohtani.
Roberts said most of the players currently preparing for the postseason are dealing with some level of physical issue.
“Most players that are performing now are not at 100%,” Roberts said.
Still, Roberts expects Ohtani to perform well when the Dodgers open their series Saturday. He also expressed confidence in Freddie Freeman, whose own lingering injuries have been a storyline heading into October, particularly after seeing Freeman in Thursday's intrasquad game.
The Dodgers will enter the NLDS with a roster expected to feature 14 position players and 12 pitchers, according to Roberts. He was not yet ready to announce the starters for Games 2 and 3.
For now, the focus belongs to Skubal.
The Dodgers acquired him to pitch in moments exactly like this one. On Saturday, in front of a home crowd and with the season entering its most important stretch, he gets the opportunity to show what he can do.
And unlike his previous playoff outings in opposing ballparks, this time, the cheers will be for him.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers hope Shohei Ohtani is better –– but are ‘not so sure’ what to expect in playoffs
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: When it comes to Shohei Ohtani’s health, the Dodgers have plenty of hope — but few precise expectations. That, at least, was the way manager Dave Roberts framed his superstar’s status on the eve of the National League Division Series on Friday, saying he was hopeful Ohtani would play well after battling right arm and left knee injuries during the second half of the season, but also acknowledging that he was “not so sure” about exactly what the slugger would be able to provide. “I know that once
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to Shohei Ohtani’s health, the Dodgers have plenty of hope — but few precise expectations.
That, at least, was the way manager Dave Roberts framed his superstar’s status on the eve of the National League Division Series on Friday, saying he was hopeful Ohtani would play well after battling right arm and left knee injuries during the second half of the season, but also acknowledging that he was “not so sure” about exactly what the slugger would be able to provide.
“I know that once the lights turn on, the postseason starts, [his] focus will be heightened,” Roberts said. “I expect good things. I really do. We just haven’t seen it enough really for me to forecast it.”
While addressing reporters on Friday for the first time since before going on the injured list in mid-September — when his injuries had become so bad he was showing visible signs of pain at the plate — Ohtani insisted his ailments had “gotten much better” and that the past few days had been “productive” for his previously slumping swing.
“I think my swing has gotten better,” he said in Japanese. “If I can make solid adjustments today, I think I can go into tomorrow in sufficient condition.”
However, Roberts also reiterated that the four-time MVP is “not 100%” following an 11-for-70 slump in his final 18 games of the regular season (the last five of which came after he returned from the IL last week).
Ohtani, meanwhile, described his injuries as something he will have to continue to manage during the playoffs, unsure if further treatment will be needed in the offseason.
During the Japanese portion of his news conference, he even revealed that, during his stint on the injured list, he avoided holding his young daughter with his aching right arm.
“I was able to hold my daughter using my left arm,” he said.
“The physical part, I think, he’s kind of moving past that,” hitting coach Aaron Bates said. “Now it’s just gaining the timing of different speeds and when he wants to get his move off, that sort of thing. Kind of the usual stuff that hitters go through, as opposed to trying to cheat [to pitches] because the physical components are limiting them.”
During the club’s bye week workouts, Ohtani took batting practice on the field multiple times — typically a rarity for him — and even sent a couple balls nearly to the outfield scoreboards, according to Bates.
“It was as good as I’ve seen it this year,” Bates said, “as far as just the way the ball was coming off [the bat].”
He also got live at-bats in the team’s intrasquad scrimmages, including a couple matchups against Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Wednesday.
“Yoshi won the matchup,” Roberts joked, but Ohtani at the very least didn’t strike out.
Whether that will be enough for Ohtani to truly turn the corner, however, remains to be seen.
For the one intrasquad scrimmage reporters were allowed to observe on Thursday, Ohtani was nowhere to be seen (staying back in the clubhouse and indoor batting cages to get his work in instead).
Ohtani himself also failed to offer much of an expectation for how he might perform this October, saying only: “I think I can get closer to the results I want if I can adjust to the atmosphere of the postseason.”
For now, such hopes will have to suffice.
Only when Game 1 of the NLDS begins on Saturday afternoon will Ohtani and the Dodgers know exactly where he is at.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dodgers Notes: Skubal Game 1, Southpaw Stategy, Sale's Status

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA—Tomorrow marks the start of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ quest for a third consecutive World Series championship, beginning with a rematch against the Atlanta Braves in the 2026 National League Division Series.
Today, both clubs hold their final workout before Saturday’s scorching mid-day opener, and we’ve got plenty of new updates and clarity on the Dodgers’ plans for the two games this weekend.
Dodgers’ NLDS Rotation Comes Into Focus With Skubal Tabbed for Game One
Leading up to the postseason, many asked what order the Dodgers would put on their star-studded starting rotation, and now we have part of an answer: two-time AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal will start Game One of the NLDS against the Braves on Saturday.
That was a shock to many, especially since 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto was considered the clear-cut favorite to lead the charge in the postseason.
The move also isn’t entirely based on the Braves’ struggles versus left-handed pitching this season; Skubal on Friday confirmed that he learned of his Game One start way back during his last outing in San Francisco, where he tossed seven shutout innings to close his 2026 regular season.
While Dave Roberts was less revealing about his outlook for Games Two and Three of the NLDS, he admitted the team would have a decision by the end of Friday’s workout, but the stars are starting to align themselves on what the likely order will be.
Yamamoto, who faced hitters on Wednesday, is now lined up to start on regular rest against the Braves during Game Three, as reported by Taro Abe of Japan’s Chunichi Sports.
That would place left-hander Blake Snell for Game Two, after Skubal and before Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow, who threw a simulated game on Thursday for a possible Game Four if needed.
There were really no “wrong” answers for Dave Roberts and the Dodgers, but this allows them to focus on the Braves’ left-handed disadvantage and decide whether to go for the series sweep or swing with their best starter, Yamamoto, on the mound in Game Three, where he’ll likely go toe-to-toe with Chris Sale.
Dodgers Look to Exploit Braves’ Left-Handed Weakness With Southpaw-Heavy Staff
After tabbed left-hander Tarik Skubal with the ball in Game One of the NLDS, it starts a running theme for the Dodgers’ plan against the Braves, and that is their inability and struggles to hit left-handed pitching.
The Braves posted just a 91 wRC+ against southpaws during the regular season, tied for 24th in MLB. They also ranked 21st in wOBA (.306), 28th in OBP (.300), and tied for 16th in batting average (.240), while their 7.0% walk rate against lefties ranked 29th.
That combination gives the Dodgers plenty of reason to load up on southpaws in the NLDS, particularly with Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell available. Skubal is already set to start Game One, giving Los Angeles a lefty right out of the gate.
Atlanta’s overall offense was productive enough to win 94 games, but its struggles against lefties provide the Dodgers with a specific weakness to attack throughout the series.
While the Dodgers have yet to announce a Game Two starter, all signs point to fellow left-hander Blake Snell, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto to follow him in Game Three at Atlanta.
As far as the Dodgers’ bullpen construction, depending on what split they have on the 26-man roster, they have plenty of left-handed options to choose from, including deadline acquisition Kris Bubic.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed Friday that the team would go with a 14-12 split for their 26-man roster, and with four starting pitchers, that leaves eight spots for the bullpen, with left-handers Tanner Scott, Jack Dreyer and Alex Vesia locked for that role.
Chris Sale Likely Out of Games One and Two as Dodgers Avoid Atlanta’s Ace Early
In an effort to push the Braves past the Phillies for their first postseason series win since the 2021 season, Chris Sale came in on two days of rest out of the bullpen to collect the final four outs of Game Three.
Despite the Braves leading 6-2 and their closer, Raisel Iglesias, available in the bullpen, new Braves skipper Walt Weiss opted for the kill shot by bringing in his best pitcher, Chris Sale.
That move, however important it was for that particular game, has changed the landscape of the Braves’ pitching plan for the NLDS, as Sale is not lined up to pitch Game One and now may not be in play for Game Two on Sunday either.
“We’re gonna err on the side of giving him (time to rest) if it’s even close… A lot of it’s going to depend on how Chris feels… Certainly don’t want to jeopardize him and his health. He just happened to feel great yesterday when he got to the park, and that’s why he was in play.”
While this could simply be Walt Weiss playing a little October gamesmanship, keeping Chris Sale away from Games One and Two would certainly give Atlanta a chance to catch the Dodgers off guard, though Dave Roberts has plenty of postseason experience himself.
Of course, Weiss could also be telling the truth. If Atlanta really plans to save Sale for his return to Truist Park, the Braves’ decision to use him in relief during Game Three of the Wild Card Series becomes even more curious.
The Braves are already down two starters in left-hander Martín Pérez and right-hander Bryce Elder, with Weiss confirming that both will not be on the NLDS roster but possibly on the NLCS roster if Atlanta advances.
That leaves the Braves with a trio of Chris Sale (down until Game Three), Tyler Mahle, and Grant Holmes, who has been used in relief as a bulk inning guy from the bullpen.
The Braves are likely to launch a bullpen game for Game One in Los Angeles on Saturday, with Mahle set to start Game Two on normal rest after a masterful outing tossing seven innings of one-run ball.
Still, the likelihood of the Dodgers seeing Sale only once this series, and as late as Game Three, is a massive advantage for Dave Roberts and Co.
Dodgers vs. Braves: How the 2026 Head-to-Head Series Shook Out
The Dodgers didn’t exactly dominate their head-to-head matchup with the Braves this season. Los Angeles went just 1-5 against Atlanta in six regular-season meetings, getting outscored 26-15 in the process.
The teams first met at Dodger Stadium from May 8th-10th, with the Dodgers taking the opener 3-1 before Atlanta won the next two games by identical 7-2 scores. The Braves then delivered an even bigger blow in the final regular-season series, sweeping Los Angeles at Truist Park from August 25th-27th. Atlanta won the opener by one run, walked off in the middle game, and finished the sweep with a 1-0 Chris Sale shutout.
This matchup also comes with some unfinished postseason business. The Dodgers and Braves last met in the 2021 NLCS, when Atlanta knocked Los Angeles out in six games before winning the World Series. The Dodgers battled back from a 2-0 series deficit to cut the deficit to one game, but the Braves slammed the door in Game Six at Truist Park.
Five years later, the two teams meet again with another trip to the NLCS on the line. After Atlanta owned the regular-season matchup, the Dodgers now have a chance to change the story when the NLDS opens Saturday at Dodger Stadium.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
Cody Snavely has been the co-editor of DodgersBeat and full-time host of the Bleed Los Podcast since February 2023. He has also written for multiple websites, such as Dodgers Way, Dodgers Low-Down, and Dodgers Tailgate. A Wilmington University graduate, Snavely is an avid Dodgers fan who uses his advanced baseball knowledge to keep fans updated on the latest storylines, rumors, and opinions on Dodgers baseball.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers name Tarik Skubal as NLDS Game 1 starter over Yoshinobu Yamamoto

item.content:encoded:
Yoshinobu Yamamoto became a Los Angeles Dodgers legend in the 2025 World Series. But he won't be the first pitcher the team trots out in this year's National League Division Series.
Instead, it will be trade deadline acquisition Tarik Skubal starting Game 1 against the Atlanta Braves on Saturday, the team announced Friday.
The Dodgers' postseason rotation consists of Skubal, Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, a high-priced and high-performing quartet, all with postseason experience. Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow were all key parts of last year's championship team, including relief appearances in Game 7 of the World Series.
Skubal, meanwhile, has a 2.04 ERA and 56 strikeouts in six career postseason starts, all in the wild-card and division rounds. The Detroit Tigers went 3-3 with him on the mound, though he only had one truly bad start in Game 5 of the 2024 ALDS against the Cleveland Guardians.
Platoon splits could have swung the decision as much as anything, as the Braves rank 11th in MLB with a .730 OPS against right-handed pitchers, like Yamamoto, compared to 21st at .696 against left-handers.
The starting decisions for Games 1 and 2 also matter quite a bit in a division series, as they also decide which pitchers are available for later in the series. Assuming the Dodgers stick to their rotation quartet, they'd go into an all-hands-on-deck Game 5 with Skubal starting and Yamamoto possibly working behind him in relief on short rest.
Both Skubal and Yamamoto were excellent in this year's regular season, with Yamamoto the only pitcher to last the entire year in the Dodgers' rotation.
Skubal, acquired at the deadline in exchange for prospects Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith, missed a month earlier this year with loose bodies in his pitching elbow but holds a 2.61 ERA with the Dodgers. No pitcher in MLB had more fWAR than him following the deadline.

item.description: 【データで見るABS制度導入による投球内容の変化】 ９月29日（日本時間30日）、ナ・リーグ地区シリーズに向けてのワークアウト日。オンライン会見に応じたロサンゼルス・ドジャースの一塁手、フレディ・フリーマンは、山本由伸の投球について聞かれ、「投げたいところへ自在に投げられるように見えます」と答え、こう続けた。 「（2024年春）初めて実戦形式の打撃練習で対戦した時から、特別な投手だと感じていました。球の質、制球力、マウンドでの落ち着き。どれもすばらしい。どんな大舞台でも、気後れすることがありません」 メジャー３年目となった今季も、山本はドジャースの先発陣を支えた。ただ、昨季と変わらず好成績を残したからといって、同じ投球を続けていたわけではない。今季のMLBでは、投手を取り巻く環境そのものが変わった。ABS（自動ボール・ストライク判定）のチャレンジ制度が導入されたからだ。 選手が球審の判定に異議を申し立てれば、ABSが即座に判定する。シーズン終盤までに5000件を超える判定が覆った。だが、ある意味でそれ以上に重要なのは、ABS導入によって、それまで球審ごとに多少の幅があったストライクゾー
item.content:encoded:
【データで見るABS制度導入による投球内容の変化】
９月29日（日本時間30日）、ナ・リーグ地区シリーズに向けてのワークアウト日。オンライン会見に応じたロサンゼルス・ドジャースの一塁手、フレディ・フリーマンは、山本由伸の投球について聞かれ、「投げたいところへ自在に投げられるように見えます」と答え、こう続けた。
「（2024年春）初めて実戦形式の打撃練習で対戦した時から、特別な投手だと感じていました。球の質、制球力、マウンドでの落ち着き。どれもすばらしい。どんな大舞台でも、気後れすることがありません」
メジャー３年目となった今季も、山本はドジャースの先発陣を支えた。ただ、昨季と変わらず好成績を残したからといって、同じ投球を続けていたわけではない。今季のMLBでは、投手を取り巻く環境そのものが変わった。ABS（自動ボール・ストライク判定）のチャレンジ制度が導入されたからだ。
選手が球審の判定に異議を申し立てれば、ABSが即座に判定する。シーズン終盤までに5000件を超える判定が覆った。だが、ある意味でそれ以上に重要なのは、ABS導入によって、それまで球審ごとに多少の幅があったストライクゾーンの判定基準が、より明確になったことだ。
特に変わったのが低めだった。今季のストライクゾーンは前年より縮小し、下端は約4.3センチ上昇したとの分析もある。低めの際どい球をストライクにしてもらうことが難しくなったのである。
これは山本にとって無関係な変化ではなかった。最大の武器のひとつが、ストライクゾーンの下へ鋭く落ちるスプリットだからだ。データサイト『ベースボール・サバント』によると、昨季42.1％だったスプリットの空振り率は今季33.8％へ低下。奪三振率も29.4％から25.7％へ下がった。
ところが、ここからが面白い。四球率は昨季の8.6％から5.9％へ大幅に改善した。一方、ストライクゾーン外の球を打者が振るチェース率は29.6％から33.9％へ上昇している。低めのストライク判定が厳密になるなか、スプリットによる空振りは減った一方で、与四球も減り、打者は以前よりボール球を振っている。ABS元年、山本は変化したストライクゾーンに合わせ、自らの投球をアジャストしていたということだ。
その過程を象徴するような時期が６月にあった。６月６日のロサンゼルス・エンゼルス戦から13日のシカゴ・ホワイトソックス戦にかけ、山本は実に45打者を連続でアウトにした。ホワイトソックス戦の８回二死、ムーキー・ベッツ遊撃手の失策で完全試合はなくなり、９回先頭のトリスタン・ピーターズの右越え本塁打でノーヒットノーランもならなかったが、投球内容は圧巻だった。
「ここ最近いい調子で来ていたので、自信を持って投げることと、とにかくストライクゾーンに思いきり投げていきました」
試合後、山本はそう振り返った。45打者連続アウトについては、興味深い言葉も返ってきた。
「いい打球も打たれながら守備に助けられたというのもありますが、前回の試合のなかですごくいい感覚で、点差があるなかでいろいろ試せたことが今日に生かせたこともありました」
山本は自身の投球技術について、試合後に細部まで説明するタイプではない。それでも「いろいろ試せた」という言葉からは、登板のなかで微調整を繰り返しながら、自分にとって最も有効な投球を探していたことがうかがえる。

item.title: [Field Level Media] Dodgers not talking 3-peat yet as Braves enter NLDS with confidence
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The potential road to history for the Los Angeles Dodgers begins with a reunion as the National League Division Series starts Saturday afternoon with a visit from the Atlanta Braves. Freddie Freeman has been a major postseason contributor during the Dodgers’ consecutive World Series titles, and the veteran will be in the heart of the order again in a matchup against his former team. Freeman also was invaluable in the 2021 World Series when the Braves won their most recent title. Fr
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The potential road to history for the Los Angeles Dodgers begins with a reunion as the National League Division Series starts Saturday afternoon with a visit from the Atlanta Braves.
Freddie Freeman has been a major postseason contributor during the Dodgers’ consecutive World Series titles, and the veteran will be in the heart of the order again in a matchup against his former team.
Freeman also was invaluable in the 2021 World Series when the Braves won their most recent title. Freeman joined the Dodgers as a free agent in 2022 after Atlanta moved on to Matt Olson as their first baseman.
While Freeman has won three rings in five seasons, the Dodgers are trying to become the first National League club to win championships in three consecutive years. Only two American League franchises have ever done it: the New York Yankees and Oakland Athletics.
The Yankees were the last to accomplish the feat when they won championships in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
“We don’t need to be adding any extra pressure onto ourselves,” Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy said. “We’ve been saying that for a long time. When you talk about three-peating, you’re putting that extra pressure on it that doesn’t need to be there. Winning a World Series is already hard enough as it is.”
After returning from a biceps injury during the final week of the regular season, Shohei Ohtani will be back atop the Los Angeles order when the club’s postseason run begins.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal was named the Dodgers’ Game 1 starter over right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Skubal arrived just before the trade deadline in a deal with the Detroit Tigers and went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA in 10 starts for his new club.
Skubal is 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA in two career starts against Atlanta, including an outing in April when he gave up two runs over seven innings in a no-decision.
The Braves opened their postseason by getting past the Philadelphia Phillies in the wild-card round. Atlanta won a winner-take-all Game 3 on Thursday behind a three-run home run from Michael Harris II and a dominating day on the mound. Six pitchers kept Philadelphia in check, including staff ace Chris Sale, who recorded the final four outs.
The Braves face the Dodgers after going 5-1 against them in the regular season, including a three-game home sweep in late August.
“Everyone knows the Dodgers have a juggernaut, but we played well against them this year,” Atlanta manager Walt Weiss said. “I know that doesn’t carry a whole lot of stock. Once the playoffs begin, everybody starts at zero. The Dodgers are healthier now than they were when we saw them.”
Weiss has yet to name his Game 1 starter, with a left-handed opener a possibility to line up against early left-handed bats like Ohtani and Freeman.
The Braves will continue to be without a pair of starters in right-hander Bryce Elder (knee) and left-hander Martin Perez (back).
Like Freeman before him, Olson has emerged as a Braves leader, along with Ronald Acuna Jr. Olson hit a team-best 41 home runs in the regular season and added another in the wild-card round. Harris hit 26 home runs in the regular season and Acuna added 20 homers and 21 steals.
“I think it’s just kind of going out there and playing our game and knowing that … we can compete with them and beat them,” said Braves catcher Drake Baldwin, an All-Star and 2025 NL Rookie of the Year who contributed 25 home runs.
–Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.title: [LAmag] Tarik Skubal, the Dodgers and the Price of October - LAmag
item.dc:creator: Camryn Rael
item.description: As the Dodgers look toward an October full of high-stakes games and another attempt to bring a World Series title back to Los Angeles, Tarik Skubal is looking a little farther ahead. After the postseason, the two-time American League Cy Young Award winner will become a free agent — and the Dodgers will have to decide how much they are willing to pay to keep him. Los Angeles acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers at the Aug. 2 trade deadline, giving up three prospects for one of baseball’s most
item.content:encoded:
As the Dodgers look toward an October full of high-stakes games and another attempt to bring a World Series title back to Los Angeles, Tarik Skubal is looking a little farther ahead. After the postseason, the two-time American League Cy Young Award winner will become a free agent — and the Dodgers will have to decide how much they are willing to pay to keep him.
Los Angeles acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers at the Aug. 2 trade deadline, giving up three prospects for one of baseball’s most accomplished starting pitchers. The Dodgers did not make the move simply to add another arm for the regular season. It was building toward October, where its goal is a third consecutive championship.
So far, the investment has paid off. Skubal posted a 2.61 ERA across 10 starts with Los Angeles and finished the regular season with seven scoreless innings against the San Francisco Giants. Now, the Dodgers are handing him the ball for Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves.
But Skubal’s October is unfolding alongside a much larger question: what happens when it ends?
Because the Dodgers acquired Skubal during the season, they did not acquire his long-term rights. He is set to enter free agency after the World Series, allowing him to negotiate with Los Angeles or any other team willing to meet his price. Players acquired in this way, shortly before free agency, are often described as “rentals” — players a team brings in for the remainder of a season with no guarantee they will return. For the Dodgers, the ideal return on that investment would be another championship. If Skubal helps deliver a third consecutive title, the prospects it gave up for a few months of his services could look like a worthwhile price.
That price could be among the largest ever for a pitcher. ESPN recently asked 27 MLB insiders to project Skubal’s next contract. Their estimates ranged from $176 million over four years to $500 million over 10 years, with an average projection of $355 million over eight years. Most of the predictions landed between $325 million and $400 million.
The clearest comparison for Dodgers fans is Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Before the 2024 season, Los Angeles signed him to a $325 million contract, setting the record for the largest guaranteed contract given to a pitcher in free agency. MLB now identifies that deal as the benchmark Skubal could surpass this offseason.
Skubal’s case for a larger contract is straightforward: he has won two consecutive Cy Young Awards and remains one of the most dominant pitchers in baseball. But there is risk in paying a 30-year-old pitcher hundreds of millions of dollars, particularly one with a history of elbow procedures. That combination — elite production and long-term uncertainty — will shape the bidding for him this winter.
Scroll to continue reading
And Skubal will not be navigating that market alone. His agent, Scott Boras, represents some of baseball’s highest-paid players and has negotiated several record-setting contracts. Boras will be responsible for helping Skubal determine not only how much he should seek, but what kind of contract makes the most sense — whether that means pursuing a shorter deal with a higher annual salary or building in options that give Skubal more control over his future. His strategy could play a significant role in determining where Skubal ultimately lands.
For now, though, Skubal’s value is being tested where the Dodgers need it most: October. His starts will give Los Angeles a closer look at what it has in the biggest games of the season — something the team will have to consider when deciding whether a long-term commitment makes sense.
But by the time the Dodgers’ season ends, the decision will no longer belong entirely to Los Angeles. Skubal and Boras will take that October experience into a market where multiple teams could be willing to pay for the same thing the Dodgers traded for in August: a top-of-the-rotation pitcher.
The Dodgers have Skubal through October. After that, they will have to decide what he is worth — and Skubal will have to decide whether their number is enough to keep him on the West Coast.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dodgers Well Represented on Year-End NL Leaderboards
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — With the end of the regular season on Sunday, the statisticians can finally put down their pencils. We had a near miss for the triple crown in the American League (Yordan Alvarez) and a pitcher with a sub-2.00 ERA in the National League (Jacob Misiorowski). And though no Dodgers were at the top of any statistically categories this year, there were plenty featured in the NL Top Ten. Let’s do a quick end-of-season rundown, shall we?
The plan for two-way dominance Cy Young/MVP consideration sort of flamed out before the All-Star break, and Shohei was struggling to find his footing at the plate in the aftermath of a couple of injuries (most notably his right knee). However, even a diminished Ohtani is among the league’s elite and Shohei did enough in the first half of the season to lock down some Top-Ten finishes. He was tied for ninth in home runs with 30, tied for tenth in walks with 81, and 19th in batting average with .275. His other numbers were also top-ten-worthy: he finished sixth in the NL in On-Base Percentage with .377 and fifth in slugging percentage with .512. And, finally, his OPS of .889 was more than 100 lower than last year, but still third in the league behind Chicago’s Pete Crow-Armstrong and the Nationals’ James Wood.
It was good year. But considering the wow factor of the first two years, a bit of a disappointment. Hopefully, he can get right in time to do damage like the old Shohei in the playoffs.
Despite his mighty struggles in September, Freddie turned in another strong campaign in 2026. Although his power number were down considerably, he still found his way on base at a clip not often seen in the modern game. Though his .288 batting average represented a low in Freddie’s Dodger years, it was still good enough for tenth place in the league. And, his 167 hits put him in eighth place in that category.
For those of you keeping track, he now stands at 2,598 hits in his career, 402 shy of the 3,000 mark that he’s had on his mind for a while. He’ll probably need three more years in the big league to reach that plateau, so that means the Dodgers would have to re-sign him after his current contract expires at the end of next year. Will that happen? It should, but I don’t know if Andrew Friedman wants to be sentimental about such things.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto was the only Dodger pitcher who logged enough innings to qualify for postseason awards, and he’s sure to get at least a sniff or two in the Cy Young voting. His year was probably his best yet: Fifth in wins (14), 3rd in ERA (2.53), 4th in innings pitched (185), 10th in strikeouts (182), 2nd in WHIP, and 2nd in Average Against (.182). Of course, all the hardwares going to the Miz this year, but Yamamoto’s steadiness is something to behold even if he doesn’t light up the radar gun on every pitch.
After a horrible year in 2025, no one was quite sure what to expect from Tanner Scott in 2026, and when Edwin Diaz went out with injury, there were more than a few Dodger fans who dreaded the thought of last year’s goat closing out games. However, Scott proved more than up to the task, converting 25 of 29 save opportunities, which put him in sixth place in the NL leader board. It will be interesting to see what happens as a resurgent Edwin Diaz seems to be ready for a return to the closer’s role.
Honorable mention….
Though they didn’t make any top tens, we should give it for Max Muncy, who made the All-Star team and finished 13th in the league in OPS and tied for 14th in the NL for homers. A really solid season from Max. Alex Vesia finished 7th in the league in appearances, and had an impact on more games than you might think. And, though they’re nowhere on the leaderboard, the strong finishes for Mookie Betts, Teoscar Hernandez, and Kyle Tucker gives one hope for the postseason.
What about the team?
Since the Dodgers won the second most games in baseball, it only figures that they’d have a lot of nice numbers at the end of the year. On the hitting side, they finished fourth in home runs (204), fourth in RBI (756), 3rd in batting average (.257), second in slugging percentage (.424), and second in OPS (.762).
On the pitching side, they finished second in team ERA (3.55), 3rd in strikeouts (1,521), first in WHIP (1.18), and first in average against (.218). When you isolate the starters, the numbers are even better: first place in ERA, WHIP, and average against, and second in strikeouts.
The bullpen was good, but closer to the middle of the pack in the NL: fourth in ERA, fourth in saves, and fourth in WHIP. One stat that may work in the pen’s favor though: they finished 14th out of 15 NL teams in bullpen innings pitched. That means that other pens (save the Phillies) have been taxed more than the Dodgers. That could make a difference the deeper we go into October.
Conclusion
The numbers show kind of how 2026 felt: it was a good year, but not a dominant year. Many players, while still contributing, were down from their historical norms. And if the past is prologue, look for a lot of low-scoring games this October. Games that might be decided by one swing of the bat or one shut-down inning.
In the meantime, we wait. We watch and we wait.
See you Saturday!
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
Now that the 2026 MLB regular season is done, Sony made one last ratings tweak for many of the players across the league on October 2. The October MLB The Show 26 ratings update saw Mookie Betts & Cade Smith rise to join the other Diamonds in the game.
The notable changes
Mookie Betts is back as a Diamond in MLB The Show 26. He and Cade Smith were the only two to move to Diamond status on October 2. Betts moved to 85 OVR after a strong final few weeks. Over his last 14 games, Betts slashed .316/.418/.632 with four home runs and 10 extra-base hits.
Smith, meanwhile, notched 41 saves and struck out 107 batters over 74 innings this season for the Guardians.
Fernando Tatis Jr. moved up three points between the last update and now. Tatis Jr., before the start of the playoffs, hit five home runs and nine extra-base hits in the last 15 games of the regular season for San Diego.
Elly De La Cruz, who had eight extra-base hits in the final two weeks, moved to 87 OVR, a +2 OVR increase. He moved there, along with NL Wild Card hero Michael Harris II.
As for who went down, Yandy Diaz and Jacob deGrom were both downgraded from Diamond status.

item.content:encoded:
【ロサンゼルス1日（日本時間2日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）が9月30日（同10月1日）の全体練習で、山本由伸投手（28）と対戦したとベイツ打撃コーチが明かした。紅白戦や実戦形式を含めても移籍後初対決で3打席の勝負だったという。また、同日まで2日連続で屋外フリー打撃も実施し、150メートル級の特大弾をマーク。同コーチは「今年1番と言っていいくらい」と状態に太鼓判を押した。
非公開練習で、大谷が衝撃の打棒を披露していた。ドジャースが戦う地区シリーズの対戦相手が東地区優勝のブレーブスに決定。報道陣に公開されたこの日の練習で、大谷はグラウンドに現れなかったが、前夜は山本との予行演習を実施し、フリー打撃では特大弾を連発したという。
「昨日はヨシと3打席対戦したよ。紅白戦に近い形だったので最終的な結果は分からない。ただ、昨日のフリー打撃は今年見た中で一番いいと言える状態だった」
9月29、30日に本拠地で開催した全体練習は非公開。30日は紅白戦が実施され、大谷は山本と3打席対戦。ドジャースではキャンプ中の実戦形式などを含めて初の実現。超一線級の球筋で実戦勘を養い、2日連続で実施した屋外フリーでは「スコアボードのすぐ下まで飛んだ打球が何本かあった」と150メートル級の放物線を放ったと証言した。
「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」による負傷者リスト（IL）から復帰後、シーズンは5試合で22打席21打数5安打8三振。実戦感覚の鈍りを感じさせる場面もあり、ロバーツ監督は地区シリーズまでに実戦形式の練習実施を要望していた。大谷にとって追い風となる可能性があるのはポストシーズンの日程。地区シリーズは最大2連戦でリーグ優勝決定シリーズ以降も最大3連戦。移動回数は増えるが、連戦が少なくコンディションを整えやすい面もある。ワールドシリーズ2連覇に貢献してきた大谷と山本。最高峰の予行演習で、戦線離脱した分の空白を埋めた。

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — He is the elephant in the lineup.
Shohei Ohtani’s presence looms large as the Dodgers prepare to open their postseason run with Game 1 of their National League Division Series on Saturday afternoon against the Atlanta Braves.
But what version of the four-time league MVP will be in the lineup on Saturday is a mystery. He has played just eight games in the past month and spoken to the media just once in the past six weeks, so assurances about his health have only come second hand.
But they have come.
“Everything is feeling great physically,” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said this week. “The swings, once he came back, overall were in a good place. And using these five days to continue to get reps and feeling good into this series is really important. But feels like he’s in a great spot.”
Ohtani returned for the final five games of the regular season and went 5 for 21 (.238) with just one extra-base hit (a double), one RBI, no runs scored, eight strikeouts and only one walk. But that was enough for Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
“I feel confident that you’re going to see the best version of Shohei of the last two months,” Roberts said, referencing a stretch that saw Ohtani hit .232 with a .745 OPS while compromised by knee and arm injuries.
“I know that’s sort of a low bar given his injury, but I do think that he’s as healthy as he’s been in quite some time, and every day from the training staff, it keeps getting better. So yeah, No. 1 he’ll be a threat being in the lineup, but I do think that the performance piece will be what we’re hoping for.”
Media were not allowed into the Dodgers’ workouts on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ohtani took batting practice on the field each day and also took three at-bats against Yoshinobu Yamamoto during Wednesday’s intrasquad game.
Thursday’s workout was open to the media and Ohtani was nowhere to be seen during batting practice or the intrasquad game that followed.
“His BP outside the last two days was really good,” Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates said during Thursday’s workout. “It was as good as we’ve seen it this year as far as the way the ball was coming off and the way he was getting his move off.
“He looked really good in his BP, in his work. He looks as good as he has as far as that goes. … The ball always comes off his bat hard, but the last two days in particular he was swinging very well.”
Bates said there have been no signs of any physical limitations in Ohtani’s work.
“The physical part he’s kind of moving past that,” Bates said. “Now it’s just getting the timing against different speeds, when he wants to get his move off, that sort of thing – kind of the usual stuff hitters go through as opposed to him navigating trying to achieve the physical components (while injured).”
The expectation is not to have Ohtani – or anyone else in the lineup – at 100% full strength, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said.
“I don’t think anyone is going to be at 100% in October,” Friedman said. “It’s a long, grueling season, and everyone’s on fumes. Our group, the team we’re playing against, everyone is on fumes. And it’s so adrenaline-based that, for me, it’s about each guy just drawing from their experience and having calmness in what they do. And I would bet on our talent to shine through.
“We don’t need anyone to try to do more.”
But they do need “a lot” from Ohtani, Roberts said, in a lineup that has underperformed at times and struggled against the better pitching staffs of the National League.
“We need him to be full strength and do what he does – take good at-bats, take what they give you,” Roberts said. “If they’re going to pitch around you to pitch to Mookie, so be it. And if they make mistakes, then hit it hard.
“Yeah, we need him to be healthy and strong. It certainly helps our offense.”

item.content:encoded:
ロサンゼルス・ドジャースの大谷翔平が、2026年のMLBポストシーズンに臨む。
本記事では、大谷翔平の2026年MLBポストシーズン出場見通しをはじめ、二刀流の可能性、ドジャースの試合日程を紹介する。
大谷翔平は2026年MLBポストシーズンに出場する？
ロサンゼルス・ドジャースの大谷翔平は、2026年のMLBポストシーズンに出場する見通しとなっている。
大谷は右上腕の炎症により9月8日付で15日間の負傷者リスト(IL)に入っていたが、9月23日(現地時間)に戦列へ復帰。復帰後も指名打者(DH)として出場を続けている。
デーブ・ロバーツ監督も「一番大事なのは健康な状態でプレーできたこと。いい状態で迎えられる」と語っており、ポストシーズンでも打者として主力出場する見通しだ。
大谷翔平はポストシーズンで二刀流出場する？
大谷の2026年シーズンにおける投手登板はすでに終了しているため、ポストシーズンでは指名打者(DH)に専念する予定となっている。
そのため、10月のポストシーズンで投手として登板する予定はなく、打者としてドジャース打線を牽引することになる。
ドジャースに所属する日本人選手
2026年のドジャースには、大谷翔平、山本由伸、佐々木朗希の日本人選手3名が所属している。
| 選手 | ポジション |
|---|---|
| 大谷翔平 | 指名打者(DH) |
| 山本由伸 | 投手 |
| 佐々木朗希 | 投手 |
ドジャースのMLBポストシーズン試合日程
ドジャースはナショナル・リーグ西地区で優勝し、第2シードを獲得したため、ワイルドカードシリーズが免除される。
ポストシーズンはナ・リーグ地区シリーズ(NLDS)から登場し、ブレーブスvsフィリーズのワイルドカードシリーズ勝者と対戦する。
ナ・リーグ地区シリーズ(NLDS)
| 試合 | 日程(日本時間) | 開催 |
|---|---|---|
| 第1戦 | 2026年10月4日(日) | ホーム |
| 第2戦 | 2026年10月5日(月) | ホーム |
| 第3戦 | 2026年10月7日(水) | アウェー |
| 第4戦 ※必要な場合 | 2026年10月8日(木) | アウェー |
| 第5戦 ※必要な場合 | 2026年10月10日(土) | ホーム |
ドジャースが地区シリーズを突破した場合の日程
ドジャースが地区シリーズを勝ち抜いた場合は、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ(NLCS)へ進出する。
NLCSは7戦4勝制で、日本時間10月12日(月)から10月20日(火)まで開催予定となっている。
さらにNLCSを突破した場合はワールドシリーズへ進出。ワールドシリーズは日本時間10月24日(土)に開幕し、最長で11月1日(日)まで行われる予定だ。
| ラウンド | 日程(日本時間) | 方式 |
|---|---|---|
| ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ(NLCS) | 2026年10月12日(月)～10月20日(火) | 7戦4勝制 |
| ワールドシリーズ(WS) | 2026年10月24日(土)～11月1日(日) | 7戦4勝制 |
MLBポストシーズン2026のテレビ放送・ネット配信予定
MLBポストシーズン2026は、Amazonプライムビデオ『SPOTVチャンネル』、『SPOTV NOW』『MLB.tv(Amazonあり)』『Lemino(SPOTVパック)』でネット配信されるほか、衛星放送『J SPORTS』でも中継が予定されている。
『NHK』でもポストシーズンの注目試合が放送される予定だ。
| チャンネル | 形態 | ポストシーズン中継 |
|---|---|---|
| SPOTVチャンネル(Amazon) [30日間無料体験あり] | ネット | ポストシーズン厳選試合、ワールドシリーズ全試合をライブ配信 【ワイルドカードシリーズ】 9/30(水)6:00 ホワイトソックスvsアストロズ 10/1(木)6:00 ホワイトソックスvsアストロズ 10/2(金)6:00 ホワイトソックスvsアストロズ 【ディビジョンシリーズ】 未発表 【リーグチャンピオンシップシリーズ】 未発表 【ワールドシリーズ】 全試合 |
| J SPORTS | 衛星放送 | 注目試合を生中継 【アストロズ vs ホワイトソックス】 9/30(水)5:50 第1戦 10/1(木)5:50 第2戦 10/2(金)5:50 第3戦 【パドレス vs カブス】 9/30(水)10:50 第1戦 10/1(木)10:50 第2戦 10/2(金)10:50 第3戦 |
| MLB.tv(Amazon) [7日間無料トライアルあり] | ネット | 全試合をライブ配信 |
| SPOTV NOW | ネット | 全試合をライブ配信 |
| Lemino(SPOTVパック) | ネット | 全試合をライブ配信 |
| NHK 総合・総合サブ | 地上波 | 注目試合を生中継 9/30(水)10:50 カブスvsパドレス |
| NHK BS | 衛星放送 | 注目試合を生中継 10/1(木)10:59 カブスvsパドレス |
| NHK BSプレミアム4K | 衛星放送 | 注目試合を生中継 9/30(水)10:50 カブスvsパドレス |
※各チャンネルの中継対象試合は各ラウンド対戦カード決定後に発表。
MLBポストシーズン2026のおすすめ視聴方法
【Amazonプライムビデオ】30日間無料体験あり
Amazonプライムビデオ『SPOTVチャンネル』では、MLB2026ポストシーズンを試合開催日に毎日1試合ライブ配信する。
プライム会員は追加料金なしで視聴でき、初めて登録する場合は30日間無料体験の利用が可能だ。
Amazonプライムビデオ登録方法
- Amazonプライムビデオのスポーツページへアクセス
- 視聴したい試合を選択
- 「ライブを観る 30日間の無料体験を始める」をタップ
- 支払い方法を入力
- 登録完了後、視聴を開始する
※無料体験終了後は月額600円(税込)で自動更新。
【SPOTV NOW】MLBポストシーズンもライブ配信
SPOTV NOW
『SPOTV NOW』では、2026シーズンもポストシーズンまでMLBを視聴できる。ポストシーズンの試合は全試合をライブ配信予定となっている。SPOTV NOW登録方法
- 「SPOTV NOW」の登録ページから希望するプランを選択
- 会員登録、またはSNSアカウント(Facebook・Apple・Yahoo!)を用いてログイン
- 各種情報を入力し、登録完了後すぐに視聴可能！
【MLB.tv】全試合配信！7日間無料体験あり
Amazon
まずはAmazonのMLB.tvチャンネルページにアクセス
- 「詳細を見る」をタップ。
- 支払い方法はクレジットカード、デビットカード、ドコモ・au・ソフトバンクの携帯決済、あと払いペイディに対応
- これで登録完了！すぐに視聴開始
なお、MLB.tvの登録は自分でキャンセルをしない限り、月額4,220円(税込)で自動更新となるので注意が必要だ。
Amazonページの「アカウントサービス」のPrime Videoチャンネルの管理からいつでもキャンセル可能だ。
※本ページは、Amazon.co.jpを宣伝しリンクすることによってサイトが紹介料を獲得できるアフィリエイトプログラムである、Amazonアソシエイト・プログラムの参加者です。

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Dodgers NLDS Notes: Edwin Díaz, Edgardo Henriquez & Starting Rotation
item.dc:creator: Matthew Moreno
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers earned the benefit of a postseason bye and now are reaping the full benefit as the Philadelphia Phillies staved off elimination to force the Atlanta Braves to a winner-take-all Game 3 in their Wild Card Series matchup. The winner advances to face the Dodgers in the National League Division Series, which begins Saturday at Dodger Stadium. The start for time for Game 1 has not yet been decided as it hinges on whether or not the San Diego Padres or Chicago Cubs reach the NLD
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers earned the benefit of a postseason bye and now are reaping the full benefit as the Philadelphia Phillies staved off elimination to force the Atlanta Braves to a winner-take-all Game 3 in their Wild Card Series matchup.
The winner advances to face the Dodgers in the National League Division Series, which begins Saturday at Dodger Stadium. The start for time for Game 1 has not yet been decided as it hinges on whether or not the San Diego Padres or Chicago Cubs reach the NLDS to play the Milwaukee Brewers.
In the meantime, the Dodgers are spending the rest of the week going through workouts and simulated games, much like their approach in 2024 that proved beneficial.
The Dodgers avoiding the Wild Card Series this year has proven beneficial for multiple players dealing with an injury, including Edgardo Henriquez.
He missed the final two weeks because of lower back discomfort but has made steady progress in his recovery and is on track for the NLDS.
“We’ll get him some work this week. He’s trending really well at this point,” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said on Tuesday. “His last live BP went well, he’s responding positively after he throws and isn’t feeling any lingering discomfort.
“We’ve still got a few steps to go, but if that all goes well, then yeah, the expectation is he’ll be on the roster.”
Elsewhere in the Dodgers bullpen, Edwin Díaz finished the regular season on a high note after returning from a stint on the 15-day injured list because of a neck issue.
“I don’t know if we could have asked much more out of Edwin. I think it was, like, a 50-plus percent strikeout rate when he came back,” Gomes noted. “Felt like each outing was more and more sharp, and looking more like himself.
“Feels like he’s in a great place right now, stuff out of hand is as good as it’s been all year, and we know that he has pitched in the hottest of hot games in the past, and in any role, especially in the postseason. He’s looked great and glad that he’s in the position that he’s in and was able to bounce back after the IL stint.”
Díaz threw five scoreless innings, allowed just one hit and one walk while collecting nine strikeouts across five appearances upon getting activated Sept. 18. While Gomes projected confidence, what may still be different for Díaz is he’s not relied upon as the primary closer.
Even without Shohei Ohtani pitching, the Dodgers are heading into the playoffs with a formidable starting rotation that consists of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. What order they will pitch in has not yet been decided.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said the team would not set their NLDS rotation until Thursday, at which point they would know whether the Braves or Phillies advanced.
“I say that because just trying to figure out opponent and the schedule going forward, not sure about game times and things like that. We’re having conversations but we’re not definitive yet,” Roberts explained.
“I think opponent certainly should matter, could matter. Talking to Mark Prior about where guys are at. To be honest, we could really put all four guys in a hat and run them out there. But I think there is going to be more thought behind it. We don’t need to make a decision right now, so really just trying to be clear and talk through it.”
Last year the Dodgers almost exclusively used Snell (Wild Card, NL Championship Series and World Series) as their Game 1 starter. Ohtani started against the Phillies in the opener of the NLDS.
One change from the 2025 postseason is Glasnow’s first appearance likely won’t come out of the bullpen during the NLDS due in part to a different schedule.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Freddie Freeman Using Bye Week to Retool His Swing for October
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Freddie Freeman knows exactly how he wants to spend the Dodgers’ five-day break before the National League Division Series. It’s all about his swing, and getting it right for the playoffs. Freeman spoke at length Tuesday about his late-season struggles, the work he plans to put in during the bye and why he feels confident he can get his swing where it needs to be by Saturday.
